Initially created: 2025-11-27T17:59:57.943+09:00 by CH Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into $lang.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the $lang translation.
5. The target language is $lang.
Input text:

p.seg: In the first year, in spring, the king's first month.
What is "first year"?
It is the prince's first year.
What is "spring"?
It is the beginning of the year.
Who is meant by "king"?
It refers to Wén Wáng.
Why is "king" mentioned before "first month"?
It is the king's first month.
What does it mean to say "king's first month"?
It signifies great unification.
Why does the Duke not speak of ascending the throne?
It fulfills the intention of Duke Chéng.
How does it fulfill the intention of the Duke?
The Duke intended to pacify the state and return it to Huán.
Why return it to Huán?
Huán was young and of noble birth,
Yǐn was older but of lower status.
The distinction between noble and base was subtle,
and the people of the state did not understand.
Yǐn was older and more virtuous,
and the senior officials supported Yǐn and established him.
Yǐn therefore declined to ascend the throne,
as it was not known that Huán would definitely be established.
Moreover, if Huán were established,
it was feared that the senior officials would be unable to assist the young ruler.
Therefore, all of Yǐn's actions in establishing himself were for the sake of establishing Huán.
Yǐn was older and more virtuous,
so why was it not appropriate for him to be established?
The heir is established based on seniority, not virtue;
the son is established based on nobility, not seniority.
How was Huán noble?
His mother was noble.
If the mother was noble, how was the son noble?
The son is noble because of the mother,
and the mother is noble because of the son.
In the third month,
the Duke and Yí Fù of Zhūlóu made a covenant at Mèi.
What does "jí (及)" mean?
It means "yǔ (與)";
"huì (會)", "jí (及)", and "jì (暨)" all mean "yǔ (與)".
Why is "huì" sometimes used,
sometimes "jí",
and sometimes "jì"?
"Huì" is like "zuì (冣)";
"jí" is like "jíjí (汲汲)";
"jì" is like "jìjì (暨暨)".
"Jí" means "I desire it";
"jì" means "it cannot be helped."
Who was Yí Fù?
He was the ruler of Zhūlóu.
Why is he referred to by his given name?
It is his zì (字).
Why is his zì used?
To commend him.
Why commend him?
Because he made a covenant with the Duke.
Many made covenants with the Duke;
why commend only this one?
He is commended because he is worthy of commendation.
How is he worthy of commendation?
He advanced gradually.
What is Mèi?
It is a borderland.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the Count of Zhèng conquered Duàn at Yān.
What does "kè (克)" mean?
It means "to kill him."
If he killed him, why is it called "kè"?
It magnifies the evil of the Count of Zhèng.
Why magnify the evil of the Count of Zhèng?
His mother wanted to establish him,
but he killed him.
It would have been better not to give him anything.
Who was Duàn?
He was the Count of Zhèng's younger brother.
Why is he not referred to as "younger brother"?
He held a fief.
What was his fief?
He held a fief.
Why is it not recorded when the people of Qí killed Wúzhī?
It happened internally.
Internally, even if he held a fief, it is not recorded;
if he did not hold a fief, even if he was outside, it is not recorded.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the King of Heaven sent Zǎi Xuān to come and deliver the gift for the funeral of Huì Gōng's Zhòngzǐ.
What is "zǎi (宰)"?
It is an office.
What is "Xuān (咺)"?
It is a name.
Why is the office used as a shì (氏)?
He was a Zǎi officer.
Who was Huì Gōng?
He was Yǐn's father.
Who was Zhòngzǐ?
She was Huán's mother.
Why is she not referred to as "fūrén (夫人)"?
Huán was not yet a ruler.
What is "fèng (賵)"?
There is "fèng" for funeral affairs.
"Fèng" generally refers to horses, teams of horses, and bundles of silk.
Carriages and horses are called "fèng,"
goods and wealth are called "fù (賻),"
clothing and bedding are called "suì (襚)."
If Huán was not yet a ruler, why did the lords come to offer "fèng"?
Yǐn was establishing Huán,
so the death of Huán's mother was announced to the lords.
Then why is it mentioned?
It fulfills the intention of Duke Chéng.
Why is "lái (來)" mentioned?
It did not involve major affairs.
Why is "Huì Gōng Zhòngzǐ" mentioned?
It combines them.
Combining them is not proper.
Why is it not mentioned regarding Zhòngzǐ?
Zhòngzǐ was insignificant.
In the ninth month,
(the Duke) and the people of Sòng made a covenant at Sù.
Who "jí (及)"-ed it?
It was an insignificant person from within.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
the Jì Bó came.
Who was the Jì Bó?
He was a grand officer of the Son of Heaven.
Why is it not said that he was sent?
He fled.
If he fled, why is it not said that he fled?
The King has no outside,
saying he fled would imply there is a place outside [the King's realm].
Gōngzǐ Yì Shī died.
Why is the day not recorded?
It was distant.
Different language is used for what is seen,
different language is used for what is heard,
and different language is used for what is transmitted. 1.2.1
In the second year, in spring,
the Duke met with the Róng at Qián.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the people of Jǔ entered Xiàng.
What does "rù (入)" mean?
It means to obtain but not reside.
Wú Hài led troops to enter Jí.
Who was Wú Hài?
He was Zhǎn Wú Hài.
Why is the shì (氏) not used?
It is a demotion.
Why is he demoted?
It is resented that annihilation began.
Did annihilation begin with this?
It happened before this.
If it happened before this, why does it begin with this?
It is merely attributed to beginning here.
Why is it attributed to beginning here?
It is the beginning of the *Chūnqiū*.
This is annihilation,
why is "rù (入)" used?
It greatly abhors internal matters, so it is avoided.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day gēngchén,
the Duke and the Róng made a covenant at Táng.
In the ninth month,
Jǐ Lǚxū came to escort the bride.
Who was Jǐ Lǚxū?
He was a *dàfū* of Jǐ.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
In wedding ceremonies, one does not refer to the host.
Then what should he be called?
He should be referred to as an uncle, elder brother, teacher, or friend.
When the Gōng of Sòng sent Gōngsūn Shòu to present betrothal gifts,
why was he referred to as the host?
Because of a lack of proper wording.
What is meant by a lack of proper wording?
It means there was no mother.
Then did Jǐ have a mother?
Yes.
If so, why was the mother not mentioned?
The mother was not in charge.
Escorting the bride is not recorded in outside states,
why is it recorded here?
To express disapproval.
What is being disapproved of?
The disapproval is for not personally welcoming the bride at the beginning.
Did the failure to personally welcome the bride begin here?
It had occurred before.
If it had occurred before, why does it start here?
It is attributed to the beginning.
Why is it attributed to the beginning?
It is the beginning of the *Chūnqiū*.
Why is a woman sometimes referred to as *nǚ* (女)?
Sometimes as *fù* (婦)?
Sometimes as *fūrén* (夫人)?
A woman is called *nǚ* in her own state,
*fù* on the way,
and *fūrén* upon entering the new state.
In the tenth month of winter,
Bó Jī was married to Jǐ.
Who was Bó Jī?
She was an inner woman (daughter of the ruler).
What does the term "married" (*guī*) mean here?
For women, getting married is called *guī*.
Jǐ Zǐbó and the Zǐ of Jǔ made a covenant at Mì.
Who was Jǐ Zǐbó?
There is no information about him.
On the day Yǐmǎo in the twelfth month,
Fūrén Zǐ Shì died.
Who was Fūrén Zǐ Shì?
She was the mother of Yǐn Gōng.
Why is her burial not recorded?
To fulfill the intention of Chéng Gōng.
How does it fulfill the intention of the Gōng?
Because the son would not ultimately become ruler,
so the mother would also not ultimately be a *fūrén*.
The people of Zhèng attacked Wèi.
In the second month of spring, the royal first month of the third year, on the day Jǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
Why is it recorded?
To record anomalies.
When there is a solar eclipse, why is it sometimes recorded with the word *rì* (日) and sometimes not?
Sometimes the word *shuò* (朔) is mentioned, and sometimes not?
When it says "on a certain month and certain day *shuò*,
there was a solar eclipse,"
it means the eclipse occurred on the first day of the month.
The reason for sometimes using *rì* and sometimes not,
and sometimes mentioning *shuò* and sometimes not,
is that sometimes it is missed before, and sometimes it is missed after.
Missing it before means the *shuò* was earlier,
missing it after means the *shuò* was later.
In the third month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Tian Wang died.
Why is the burial not recorded?
The death of the Son of Heaven is recorded, but not the burial,
because it must be at the right time.
The death and burial of feudal lords are recorded
because when the Son of Heaven is alive,
they cannot necessarily be at the right time.
Why are the words *bēng* (崩) and *hōng* (薨) used differently?
The Son of Heaven's death is called *bēng*,
a feudal lord's death is called *hōng*,
a *dàfū*'s death is called *zú* (卒),
and a *shì*'s death is called *bùlù* (不祿).
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Yǐn Shì died.
Who was Yǐn Shì?
He was a *dàfū* of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as Yǐn Shì?
It is a demotion.
Why is it a demotion?
It criticizes hereditary officialdom,
and hereditary officialdom is not in accordance with propriety.
The death of an outside *dàfū* is not recorded,
so why is it recorded here?
The Tiān Wáng died, and he was the master of the feudal lords.
In autumn,
Wǔ Shì Zǐ came to request a funeral grant.
Who was Wǔ Shì Zǐ?
He was a *dàfū* of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as Wǔ Shì Zǐ?
It is a criticism.
What is being criticized?
The father died, but the son had not yet been appointed.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
Because he was still in mourning and not yet a ruler.
Why is the fact that Wǔ Shì Zǐ came to request a funeral grant recorded?
To express disapproval.
What is being disapproved of?
In mourning affairs, one should not request anything.
Requesting a funeral grant is not in accordance with propriety
and probably involved collusion with inferiors.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngchén,
Sòng Gōng Hé died.
In the twelfth month of winter,
the Hóu of Qí and the Bó of Zhèng made a covenant at Shímén.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Mù Gōng of Sòng was buried.
Why is the burial sometimes recorded with the day and sometimes not?
Recording the day when it is not the appropriate time indicates a hasty burial.
Not recording the day when it is not the appropriate time indicates a slow burial.
Recording the day when it is past the appropriate time conceals something.
Not recording the day when it is past the appropriate time indicates an inability to perform the burial.
Not recording the day at the appropriate time is correct.
Recording the day at the appropriate time indicates a dangerous inability to perform the burial.
What was the danger at the appropriate time in this case?
Xuān Gōng said to Mù Gōng:
"If it were based on my love for my daughter,
it would be better to love Yí.
But if it is based on who should be the master of the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temples,
then Yí is not as good as my daughter.
Why not make her the ruler in the end?"
When Xuān Gōng died,
Mù Gōng became the ruler.
Mù Gōng drove away his two sons, Zhuāng Gōng Féng and Zuǒ Shī Bó,
saying:
"As my sons,
do not see each other in life,
and do not weep for each other in death."
Yǔ Yí then said:
"The reason why the former ruler did not give the state to his son but entrusted the state to you
was because he believed that you could be the master of the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temples.
Now, you have driven away your two sons and intend to give the state to Yǔ Yí.
This is not what the former ruler intended.
Moreover, if sons can be driven away,
then the former ruler would have driven away his minister."
Mù Gōng said:
"It is clear that the former ruler would not have driven you away,
as I am standing here as a regent."
In the end, he gave the state to Yǔ Yí.
Zhuāng Gōng Féng assassinated Yǔ Yí.
Therefore, a *jūnzǐ* greatly values holding to what is correct.
The disaster of Sòng was caused by Xuān Gōng.
In the second month of spring, the royal first month of the fourth year,
the people of Jǔ attacked Qǐ
and took Móulóu.
What was Móulóu?
It was a town of Qǐ.
The taking of a town of an outside state is not recorded,
so why is it recorded here?
To express disapproval of the initial taking of a town.
On the day Wùshēn,
Zhōu Xū of Wèi assassinated his ruler Wán.
Why is the state name used?
Because he held the state.
In summer,
the Gōng and the Gōng of Sòng met at Qīng.
What is meant by "met" (*yù*)?
It means unexpectedly.
One ruler went out,
and the other ruler went to meet him.
The Gōng of Sòng, the Hóu of Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
1.4.5 In autumn,
Huī led the army to join with Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi to attack Zhèng.
Who is Huī?
It is Gōngzǐ Huī.
Why is he not called Gōngzǐ?
It is a demotion.
Why is it a demotion?
Because of his involvement in the assassination of the ruler.
How was he involved in the assassination of the ruler?
Gōngzǐ Huī flattered Yǐngōng,
saying to Yǐngōng:
"The people are at peace with you,
the lords are pleased with you,
why not become the ruler once and for all?"
Yǐn said:
"I will not,
I will send Xiūtú Qiú,
I will grow old there."
Gōngzǐ Huī feared that his words would be heard by Huán,
so he said to Huán:
"I have spoken for you to Yǐn.
Yǐn said:
'I will not go back on my word.'"
Huán said:
"Then what should be done?"
He said:
"Please create a difficulty
and assassinate Yǐngōng."
He assassinated Yǐngōng at the sacrifice to Zhōng Wū.
1.4.6 In the ninth month,
the people of Wèi killed Zhōu Xū in Pú.
Why is he referred to as a "person"?
It is a term used to denounce a traitor.
1.4.7 In the twelfth month of winter,
the people of Wèi installed Jìn.
Who is Jìn?
It is Gōngzǐ Jìn.
What does "installed" mean?
"Installed" means that it was not proper to install him.
Why is he referred to as a "person"?
It is a way of saying that the masses installed him.
Then who installed him?
Shí Què installed him.
If Shí Què installed him,
then why is he referred to as a "person"?
It means that he was whom the masses desired to install.
Even though the masses desired to install him,
his installation was improper.
1.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring,
the Duke watched fish at Táng.
Why is this written?
It is a criticism.
What is the criticism?
Distance.
Why did the Duke go far to watch fish?
It was to receive Dēng Lái.
The Duke spread a hundred gold pieces for the fish.
What does "receiving Dēng Lái" mean?
It is a term to praise his great beauty.
What is Táng?
It is a city on the Jǐ River.
1.5.2 In the fourth month of summer,
the funeral of Huángōng of Wèi took place.
1.5.3 In autumn,
the army of Wèi entered Shèng.
Why do some say "led the army" and others not say "led the army"?
When honoring a respected and numerous army, it is said that so-and-so "led the army";
when honoring a respected but small army, it is said that so-and-so was the "commander";
when belittling a numerous army, it is said "the army";
when belittling a small army, it is said "the people."
The ruler's army does not use "led the army";
it records what is most important.
1.5.4 In the ninth month,
they examined Zhòngzǐ's palace.
What is "examining the palace"?
"Examining" is like entering the room,
beginning the sacrifice to Zhòngzǐ.
If Huán was not yet the ruler, then why was he sacrificing to Zhòngzǐ?
Yǐn established Huán,
so he sacrificed to his mother for Huán.
Then what does it mean?
It fulfills the intentions of the Duke.
Initially, six *yǔ* dancers were offered.
What does "initially" mean?
It means "beginning."
What are "six *yǔ*" dancers?
They are dancers.
Why is the initial offering of six *yǔ* dancers written?
It is a criticism.
What is the criticism?
It criticizes the beginning of usurping the rites of the dukes.
How is "six *yǔ*" dancers a usurpation?
The Son of Heaven has eight rows,
the dukes have six,
and the lords have four.
What are the "dukes"?
What are the "lords"?
The three chief ministers of the Son of Heaven are called "dukes";
the descendants of kings are called "dukes";
the remaining large states are called "lords";
and small states are called "earls, viscounts, or barons."
What are the "three chief ministers of the Son of Heaven"?
They are the advisors of the Son of Heaven.
If they are advisors of the Son of Heaven, then why are there three?
The Zhōu prince is in charge of those east of Shǎn;
the Shào prince is in charge of those west of Shǎn;
and one advisor resides within.
Did the usurpation of the dukes begin here?
It was before this.
If it was before this, then why did it begin here?
Usurping the rites of the dukes can still be spoken of;
usurping the rites of the Son of Heaven cannot be spoken of.
1.5.5 The people of Zhūlóu and the people of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
1.5.6 Locusts.
Why is this written?
To record a disaster.
1.5.7 In the twelfth month of winter, on *xīnsì*,
Gōngzǐ Kōu died.
1.5.8 The people of Sòng attacked Zhèng,
and besieged Chánggé.
Cities are not described as being besieged;
why is "besieged" used here?
It indicates the strength of the attack.
1.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
the people of Zhèng came to surrender peace.
What is "surrendering peace"?
"Surrendering peace" is like destroying what has been accomplished.
Why is it said that they "destroyed what has been accomplished"?
They ruined their accomplishments.
They said, "Our accomplishments are ruined."
We did not achieve anything with the people of Zhèng.
If we did not achieve anything with the people of Zhèng, then why did we not achieve anything?
In the battle of Hú Rǎng,
Yǐngōng gained a victory.
Then why is the battle not mentioned?
It is to avoid mentioning the victory.
1.6.2 In the fifth month of summer, on *xīnyǒu*,
the Duke met with Hóu of Qí and formed an alliance at Ài.
In the seventh month of autumn.
Why is this written when nothing happened?
Although nothing happened in the *Chūnqiū*,
the beginning of a season is recorded if it passes.
Why is the beginning of a season recorded when it passes?
The *Chūnqiū* is organized by year;
only when the four seasons are complete is it considered a year.
1.6.3 In winter,
the people of Sòng took Chánggé.
The capture of a city from the outside is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
Because it took a long time.
1.7.1 In the seventh year, in the third month of spring,
Shū Jī returned to Jǐ.
Hóu of Téng died.
Why is his name not mentioned?
Because it was a small state.
If it was a small state, then why is he called a "Hóu"?
There is no conflict.
In the *Chūnqiū*, noble and humble are not distinguished by the same titles,
and good and bad are not distinguished by the same words.
1.7.2 In summer,
they walled Zhōng Qiū.
What is Zhōng Qiū?
It is an inner city.
Why is the walling of Zhōng Qiū recorded?
It is recorded to emphasize its importance.
1.7.3 Hóu of Qí sent his younger brother Nián to come for a formal visit.
Why is he called "younger brother"?
A younger brother by the same mother is called "younger brother,"
and an older brother by the same mother is called "older brother."
1.7.4 In autumn,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu.
Winter,
the Heavenly King sent Fán Bó to come for a formal visit.
The Róng attacked Fán Bó at Chǔqiū and
took him away.
Who was Fán Bó?
He was a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
This was a formal visit,
why does it say "attacked"?
It means captured.
If it means captured, then why does it say "attacked"?
To emphasize it.
Why emphasize it?
Because they didn't want the Yí and Dí to capture someone from the central states.
What was its location?
To emphasize it.
Eighth year, spring,
the Lord of Sòng and the Marquis of Wèi met at Chuí.
Third month,
Bó of Zhèng sent Wǎn to return Bǐng.
Who was Wǎn?
A minor figure from Zhèng.
What was Bǐng?
A bathing town of Zhèng.
When the Son of Heaven had affairs at Tài Mountain,
all the lords followed.
Below Tài Mountain,
all the lords had bathing towns there.
On gēng-yín,
we entered Bǐng.
Why does it say "entered"?
It was difficult.
What about the day?
It was difficult.
Why does it say "we"?
Saying "we" doesn't only mean us,
Qí also wanted it.
Summer, sixth month, jǐ-hài,
the Marquis Kǎofù of Cài died.
xīn-hài,
the Viscount of Sù died.
Autumn, seventh month, gēng-wǔ,
the Lord of Sòng, the Marquis of Qí, and the Marquis of Wèi made a covenant at Wǎwū.
Eighth month,
the Duke Xuān of Cài was buried.
Why is the death recorded with his name but the burial is not?
The death follows correctness,
while the burial follows the host.
Why is the death recorded with the day but the burial is not?
The death is reported immediately, but the burial is not announced.
Ninth month, xīn-mǎo,
the Duke and the people of Jǔ made a covenant at Bāolái.
Why did the Duke make a covenant with minor people?
When "people" is mentioned, it is without doubt.
Locusts.
Winter, twelfth month,
Wú Hài died.
This was Zhǎn Wú Hài.
Why isn't his clan name mentioned?
Because the disease had just begun to abate,
therefore he wasn't given a clan name for his entire life.
Ninth year, spring,
the Heavenly King sent Nán Jì to come for a formal visit.
Third month, guǐ-yǒu,
there was heavy rain with thunder and lightning.
Why is it recorded?
To record something unusual.
What was unusual about it?
It was out of season.
gēng-chén,
there was heavy snow.
Why is it recorded?
To record something unusual.
What was unusual about it?
It was excessively large.
Xiá died.
Who was Xiá?
He was one of our senior officials who had not yet received a commission.
Summer,
the walls of Láng were built.
Autumn, seventh month.
Winter,
the Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Bǐng.
Tenth year, spring, royal second month,
the Duke met the Marquis of Qí and the Count of Zhèng at Zhōngqiū.
Summer,
Huī led an army to join the people of Qí and the people of Zhèng to attack Sòng.
This was Gōngzǐ Huī,
why isn't he called Gōngzǐ?
It is a demotion.
Why is he demoted?
He concealed the crimes of Yǐn.
Therefore, he is demoted throughout the chapter on Yǐn.
Sixth month, rén-xū,
the Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Jiān.
On xīn-wèi he took Gào,
on xīn-sì he took Fáng.
Taking cities is not recorded by day,
so why is it recorded by day here?
Because they were taken twice in one month.
Why mention that they were taken twice in one month?
To emphasize it.
Great evils within are concealed,
so why is it emphasized here?
The *Chūnqiū* records internal matters but omits external matters;
great evils outside are recorded,
while small evils are not recorded;
great evils inside are concealed,
while small evils are recorded.
Autumn,
the people of Sòng and the people of Wèi entered Zhèng.
The people of Sòng, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi attacked Zài,
and the Count of Zhèng attacked and took it.
Why does it say "attacked and took it"?
It was easy.
Why was it easy?
Because of their strength.
Whose strength?
The strength of the people of Sòng, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi.
Winter, tenth month, rén-wǔ,
the people of Qí and the people of Zhèng entered Shèng.
Eleventh year, spring,
the Marquis of Téng and the Marquis of Xuē came to court.
Why does it say "came to court"?
When lords come, it is called "attending court";
when senior officials come, it is called "formal visit".
Why are both terms used together?
Because they are minor states.
Summer, fifth month,
the Duke met the Count of Zhèng at Qílí.
Autumn, seventh month, rén-wǔ,
the Duke, the Marquis of Qí, and the Count of Zhèng entered Xǔ.
Winter, eleventh month, rén-chén,
the Duke died.
Why isn't the burial recorded?
It is concealed.
Why conceal it?
Because he was murdered.
If he was murdered, then why isn't the burial recorded?
In the *Chūnqiū*, if a lord is murdered and the traitor is not punished,
the burial is not recorded,
because it is considered that he has no subjects.
Zǐ Shěnzi said:
"If a lord is murdered
and the subject does not punish the traitor,
he is not a subject.
If a son does not avenge his father,
he is not a son.
Burial is the affair of the living.
In the *Chūnqiū*, if a lord is murdered and the traitor is not punished,
the burial is not recorded,
because it is considered that it is not connected to the subjects."
Why doesn't it mention the place when the Duke died?
Because they couldn't bear to say it.
Why doesn't Yǐn have a first month?
Because Yǐn was going to yield to Huán,
therefore he didn't possess his own first month.
2.1.1 In the first year, spring, the king's first month,
the Duke ascended the throne.
Having succeeded a ruler who was murdered, it is not said that he ascended the throne.
Why is it said here that he ascended the throne?
It accords with his intention.
In the third month,
the Duke met with Zhèng Bó at Chuí.
Zhèng Bó used bì jade to lease Xǔ field.
Why does it say he used bì to lease it?
It was to exchange it.
If it was to exchange it, why does it say he leased it?
It was to show respect.
Why show respect?
Because while the Son of Heaven exists,
the feudal lords are not allowed to exclusively possess land.
What is Xǔ field?
It is an邑(yì) where the Lǔ court stayed overnight.
When the feudal lords paid court to the Son of Heaven,
in the suburbs of the Son of Heaven,
the feudal lords all had邑(yì) for overnight stays.
Since this was an邑(yì) where the Lǔ court stayed overnight,
why is it called Xǔ field?
It avoids mentioning taking land from the Zhōu.
If it avoids mentioning taking land from the Zhōu,
why is it called Xǔ field?
It is connected to Xǔ.
Why connect it to Xǔ?
Because it is near Xǔ.
Since this is an邑(yì),
why is it called a field?
When there is more field than邑(yì), it is called a field;
when there is more邑(yì) than field, it is called an邑(yì).
In summer, the fourth month, on the day of Dīngwèi,
the Duke and Zhèng Bó formed an alliance at Yuè.
In autumn, there was a great flood.
Why is this recorded?
To record a disaster.
In winter, the tenth month.
In the second year, spring, the king's first month, on the day of Wùshēn,
Sòng Dū murdered his lord Yǔ Yí and his grand master Kǒng Fù.
What does "及(jí)" mean?
It means "involved."
There have been many murders of rulers,
are there none others involved besides this one?
It is said: there are.
Chóu Mù and Xún Xī were both involved.
Were there none others involved besides Chóu Mù and Xún Xī?
It is said: there are.
If there are others, why is this one recorded?
Because of his worthiness.
What was worthy about Kǒng Fù?
Kǒng Fù can be said to have embodied righteousness in his appearance.
How did his righteousness manifest in his appearance?
Dū was about to murder Shāng Gōng;
if Kǒng Fù lived and was present, then Shāng Gōng could not be murdered,
therefore, he first attacked Kǒng Fù's house.
Shāng Gōng knew that if Kǒng Fù died, he would certainly die,
so he rushed to save him,
and they both died there.
Kǒng Fù stood upright in the court with a stern expression,
so that no one dared to overstep and bring trouble to his lord;
Kǒng Fù can be said to have embodied righteousness in his appearance.
Téng Zǐ came to court.
In the third month,
the Duke met with Qí Hóu, Chén Hóu, and Zhèng Bó at Jì
in order to settle the unrest in Sòng.
Internal great evils are avoided,
so why is it mentioned here in detail?
Because it was distant.
What was seen is described differently,
what was heard is described differently,
and what was passed down is described differently.
Yǐn was also distant,
so why was it concealed?
Because Duke Yǐn was worthy, and Duke Huán was base.
In summer, the fourth month,
the great Dǐng cauldron of Gào was taken from Sòng.
Since it was taken from Sòng,
why is it called the Gào Dǐng?
Utensils follow their names,
and land follows its owner.
How do utensils follow their names?
How does land follow its owner?
Utensils and people
are not immediately possessed.
Sòng initially took it unjustly,
so it is called the Gào Dǐng.
However, the relationship between land and people is different;
after a while, it can be possessed.
Then can taking something allow one to possess it?
It is said: no.
Why?
Like the wife of the king of Chǔ, Wèi,
there is no time when it is permissible.
On the day of Wùshēn,
it was placed in the great temple.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
Proceeding to disorder by accepting bribes,
and placing it in the great temple
is not in accordance with ritual.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Jǐ Hóu came to court.
Cài Hóu and Zhèng Bó met at Dèng;
when apart, it is not said they met,
so why is it said here that they met?
Because Dèng participated in the meeting.
In the ninth month,
they entered Qǐ.
The Duke and the Róng formed an alliance at Táng.
In winter,
the Duke returned from Táng.
In the third year, spring, the first month,
the Duke met with Qí Hóu at Yíng.
In summer,
Qí Hóu and Wèi Hóu exchanged commands at Pú.
What does "胥命(xū mìng)" mean?
It means "exchanging commands."
Why is it said they exchanged commands?
Because it was close to being correct.
How was this close to being correct?
In ancient times, they did not form alliances,
but made verbal agreements and withdrew.
In the sixth month,
the Duke met with Jǐ Hóu at Shèng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Rénchén,
there was a solar eclipse,
complete.
What does "既(jì)" mean?
It means "complete."
Gōngzǐ Huī went to Qí to escort the bride.
In the ninth month,
Qí Hóu escorted Jiāng Shì to Huān.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
That the feudal lords crossed the border to escort a woman
is not in accordance with ritual.
Although she has entered the country,
why is she not referred to as "夫人(fū rén)" (Lady)?
From my perspective as Qí,
parents in relation to their son,
even if she is the lady of a neighboring state,
would still say, "my Jiāng Shì."
The Duke met with Qí Hóu at Huān,
and Lady Jiāng Shì arrived from Qí.
Why didn't Huī escort her?
Because she had already been received by the Duke.
In winter,
Qí Hóu sent his younger brother Nián to pay a formal visit.
There was a harvest.
Why is "有年(yǒu nián)" (there was a harvest) recorded?
It is recorded with joy.
Why is "大有年(dà yǒu nián)" (there was a great harvest) recorded?
It is also recorded with joy.
Why does this say "有年(yǒu nián)" (there was a harvest)?
Because it was only a moderate harvest.
Why does that say "大有年(dà yǒu nián)" (there was a great harvest)?
Because it was a great harvest.
Is a moderate harvest also sufficient to warrant joy?
One relies on having a harvest.
In the first month of spring in the fourth year,
the Duke hunted at Láng (郎).
What is "hunting"?
It is field hunting.
In spring it is called miáo (苗),
in autumn it is called sōu (蒐),
in winter it is called shòu (狩).
Ordinary events are not recorded,
why is this recorded?
Criticism.
What is criticized?
Its remoteness.
Why must the feudal lords conduct field hunts?
First, for gāndòu (乾豆);
second, for guests;
third, to replenish the ruler's kitchen.
In summer,
the Heavenly King sent Zǎi Qú Bó Jiū (宰渠伯糾) to pay a formal visit.
Who is Zǎi Qú Bó Jiū (宰渠伯糾)?
He is a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as Zǎi Qú Bó Jiū (宰渠伯糾)?
He is a junior official.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year, on jiǎxū (甲戌) and jǐchǒu (己丑),
the Marquis Bào (鮑) of Chén (陳) died.
Why are two days given?
For the grief of his death.
He disappeared on the day of jiǎxū (甲戌),
and on the day of jǐchǒu (己丑) he was found dead.
The gentlemen were in doubt about it,
therefore, his death was recorded with two days.
In summer,
the Marquis of Qí (齊) and the Count of Zhèng (鄭) went to Jǐ (紀).
External mutual visits are not recorded,
why is this recorded?
Their departure is not called a meeting.
The Heavenly King sent the son of Réng Shū (仍叔) to pay a formal visit.
Who is the son of Réng Shū (仍叔)?
He is a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as the son of Réng Shū (仍叔)?
Criticism.
What is criticized?
It is a criticism of fathers being old and sons succeeding them in government.
The funeral of Duke Huán (桓) of Chén (陳).
The construction of the city of Zhùqiū (祝丘).
In autumn,
the people of Cài (蔡), the people of Wèi (衛), and the people of Chén (陳) followed the King to attack Zhèng (鄭).
Why does it say "followed the King to attack Zhèng (鄭)"?
Following the King is proper.
A grand yǔ (雩) sacrifice.
What is a grand yǔ (雩) sacrifice?
It is a drought sacrifice.
Then why is drought not mentioned?
Speaking of yǔ (雩) means drought is seen, speaking of drought means yǔ (雩) is not seen.
How is it written?
It records a disaster.
Locusts.
Why is it written?
It records a disaster.
In winter,
the Duke of Zhōu (州) went to Cáo (曹).
External mutual visits are not recorded,
why is this recorded?
He passed by us.
In the first month of spring in the sixth year,
Shí (寔) came.
What does "Shí (寔) came" mean?
It is like saying, "This person came."
Who is it referring to?
It is referring to the Duke of Zhōu (州).
Why is it called "Shí (寔) came"?
It is disrespectful to him.
Why is it disrespectful to him?
He has transformed us.
In the fourth month of summer,
the Duke met with Marquis Jǐ (紀) at Chéng (成).
In the eighth month of autumn, on rénwǔ (壬午),
a grand review.
What is a grand review?
It is an inspection of chariots.
Why is it recorded?
Because it is rarely recorded.
The people of Cài (蔡) killed Chén Tuó (陳佗).
Who is Chén Tuó (陳佗)?
He is the ruler of Chén (陳).
If he is the ruler of Chén (陳), then why is he called Chén Tuó (陳佗)?
It is a severance.
Why is he severed?
It is contemptible.
How is he contemptible?
He was promiscuous abroad.
Where was he promiscuous?
He was promiscuous in Cài (蔡),
and the people of Cài (蔡) killed him.
In the ninth month, on dīngmǎo (丁卯),
Zǐ Tóngshēng (子同生) was born.
Who is Zǐ Tóngshēng (子同生)?
It is referring to Duke Zhuāng (莊).
Why is it said that Zǐ Tóngshēng (子同生) was born?
It is a joy at having a legitimate heir.
There has been no mention of joy at having a legitimate heir,
why is there this mention of joy at having a legitimate heir?
It is because there has been no legitimate heir for a long time.
Master Gōngyángzǐ (公羊子) said:
“Is it perhaps to distress Duke Huán (桓)?”
In winter,
Marquis Jǐ (紀) came to court.
In the second month of spring in the seventh year, on jǐhài (己亥),
Xiánqiū (咸丘) was burned.
Why was it burned?
It was being burned for firewood.
Why was it being burned for firewood?
It was an attack with fire.
Why is it said to be an attack with fire?
It records the first attack with fire.
What is Xiánqiū (咸丘)?
It is a city of Zhūlóu (邾婁).
Why is it not associated with Zhūlóu (邾婁)?
It is being treated as a state.
Why is it being treated as a state?
The ruler resided there.
In summer,
Bó Suí (伯綏), the Earl of Gǔ (穀), came to court.
Hóu Wúlí (侯吾離), the Marquis of Dèng (鄧), came to court.
Why are they both named?
They are rulers who have lost their territories.
Why are they called "Marquis" when they come to court?
The noble ones have no successors,
they are treated as if they were in the beginning.
In the first month of spring in the eighth year, on jǐmǎo (己卯),
a zhēng (烝) sacrifice.
What is a zhēng (烝) sacrifice?
It is a winter sacrifice.
In spring it is called cí (祠),
in summer it is called yuè (礿),
in autumn it is called cháng (嘗),
in winter it is called zhēng (烝).
Ordinary events are not recorded,
why is this recorded?
Criticism.
What is criticized?
It is criticized for being frequent.
Frequency leads to excess,
excess leads to disrespect.
The gentlemen's sacrifices are
respectful but not excessive.
Remissness leads to laziness,
laziness leads to forgetting.
If an official does not meet these four conditions,
then in winter he will not have fur clothing,
and in summer he will not have linen clothing.
The Heavenly King sent Jiāfù (家父) to pay a formal visit.
In the fifth month of summer, on dīngchǒu (丁丑),
a zhēng (烝) sacrifice.
Why is it recorded?
It is criticized for being frequent.
In autumn,
an attack on Zhūlóu (邾婁).
In the tenth month of winter,
rain and snow.
Why is it recorded?
It records an anomaly.
What is anomalous about it?
It is out of season.
Jì Gōng came,
and then welcomed the queen from Jǐ.
Who is Jì Gōng?
One of the three dukes of the Son of Heaven.
Why isn't he referred to as an envoy?
In wedding ceremonies, the host is not referred to.
What does "then" (遂) mean?
To initiate an affair.
A senior officer (dàfū) does not initiate affairs;
why does it say "then" here?
Completing an errand for me.
How is it completing an errand for me?
Making me the matchmaker;
if it's acceptable, then accordingly use this to go and welcome her.
In her own state, she is called a daughter;
why is she called the queen here?
The King has no outside (state),
its wording is accomplished.
2.9.1 In the ninth
year, in spring,
Jì Jī Jiāng returned to the capital.
Its wording is accomplished;
then why is she called Jì Jī Jiāng?
From my perspective, speaking of Jì,
regarding parents and their child,
even if she becomes queen of the Son of Heaven,
they would still say, "My Jī Jiāng."
What is the capital?
The residence of the Son of Heaven.
What does "capital" (京, jīng) mean?
Great.
What does "city" (師, shī) mean?
Multitude.
The residence of the Son of Heaven
must be spoken of with terms of multitude and greatness.
Summer, fourth month.
Autumn, seventh month.
Winter,
Bó of Cáo sent his heir apparent Shègū to court.
When the feudal lords come, it is called a court visit (朝, cháo);
this is the heir apparent;
why is it called a court visit?
The *Chūnqiū* criticizes those who are old fathers or sons who take over the government;
then does it not know whether it is in Qí
or Cáo?
Tenth year, spring, royal first month, *gēngshēn*,
Cáo Bó Zhōngshēng passed away.
Summer, fifth month,
the funeral of Duke Huán of Cáo.
Autumn,
the duke met with the Marquis of Wèi at Táoqiū,
but did not encounter him.
What does "meet" (會, huì) mean?
A term of appointment.
Why does it say "did not encounter"?
The duke was not wanted.
Winter, twelfth month, *bǐngwǔ*,
the Marquis of Qí, the Marquis of Wèi, and Bó of Zhèng came to fight at Láng.
What is Láng?
Our nearby city.
If it is our nearby city, then why does it say, "came to fight at Láng"?
Near.
Near to what?
Near to being besieged.
This is a partial battle;
why is it not said that the army was utterly defeated?
Internally, battles are not mentioned;
if battle is mentioned, then it is a defeat.
Eleventh year, spring, first month,
the people of Qí, the people of Wèi, and the people of Zhèng made a covenant at Ècáo.
Summer, fifth month, *guǐwèi*,
Bó of Zhèng, Wùshēng, passed away.
Autumn, seventh month,
the funeral of Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng.
Ninth month,
the people of Sòng seized Jì Zhòng of Zhèng.
Who is Jì Zhòng?
The chancellor of Zhèng.
Why is his name not mentioned?
Because he was worthy.
How was Jì Zhòng worthy?
Because he was considered to know authority.
How did he know authority?
In ancient times, the state of Zhèng was located at Liú.
The former Bó of Zhèng had a good relationship with the Duke of Kuài,
colluded with the duke's wife to take his state,
and moved Zhèng there,
and abandoned Liú.
Duke Zhuāng died
and was buried.
Jì Zhòng was about to go visit Liú,
and on the road he went through Sòng,
and the people of Sòng seized him.
They said to him,
"For us, depose Hū and establish Tū."
If Jì Zhòng did not follow their words,
then the lord would surely die,
and the state would surely perish.
If he followed their words,
then the lord could exchange life for death,
and the state could exchange survival for destruction.
Slightly delaying and easing things,
then Tū could be legitimately deposed,
and Hū could be legitimately returned;
if this was not attainable, then fall ill,
and then there would be a state of Zhèng.
For the ancients who had authority,
Jì Zhòng's authority is an example.
What is authority?
Authority is the reversal of the norm,
and then there is goodness.
Where authority is established,
there is nothing established other than abandoning death.
There is a way to exercise authority;
demeaning oneself to exercise authority,
not harming others to exercise authority;
killing others to sustain oneself,
destroying others to preserve oneself,
the virtuous do not do it.
Tū returned to Zhèng.
Why is Tū named?
Because of the connection with Jì Zhòng.
Why does it say "returned"?
Because he obeyed Jì Zhòng.
Zhèng Hū fled to Wèi.
Why is Hū named?
In the *Chūnqiū*, duke, son, and man are all the same;
the wording is without any degradation.
Róu met with Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, and Uncle of Cài to make a covenant at Zhé.
Who is Róu?
An officer (dàfū) of ours who has not yet been appointed.
The duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Fūtóng.
*Eleventh Year of Duke Huán*
2.11.8 Winter, twelfth month, the duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Kàn.
Twelfth year, spring, first month.
Summer, sixth month, *rén yín*,
the duke met with the Marquis of Jǐ and the Viscount of Jǔ,
and made a covenant at Ōushé.
Autumn, seventh month, *dīng hài*,
the duke met with the Duke of Sòng and the people of Yān, and made a covenant at Gǔqiū.
Eighth month, *rén chén*,
Marquis Yuè of Chén passed away.
The duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Tán.
Winter, eleventh month,
the duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Guī.
*Bǐngxū*,
the duke met with Bó of Zhèng,
and made a covenant at Wǔfǔ.
*Bǐngxū*,
Marquis Jìn of Wèi passed away.
Twelfth month,
along with the army of Zhèng, they attacked Sòng.
*Dīngwèi*,
they fought in Sòng.
If there is a battle, it is not called an attack;
why does it say "attack" here?
To avoid suspicion.
Suspect of what?
Suspect of fighting with the people of Zhèng.
This is a partial battle;
why is it not said that the army was utterly defeated?
Internally, battles are not mentioned;
if battle is mentioned, then it is a defeat.
2.13.1 In the second month of spring in the thirteenth year,
Gōng met with Hóu of Jǐ and Bó of Zhèng.
Jǐsì,
they fought with Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, and the people of Yān.
The troops of Qí, the troops of Sòng, the troops of Wèi, and the troops of Yān were utterly defeated.
Why did they set a later date?
They relied on outside forces.
How did they rely on outside forces?
Only by obtaining Hóu of Jǐ and Bó of Zhèng could they set a date.
Inside, it does not mention the battle.
Why does this mention the battle?
It was from outside.
Why from outside?
Because they relied on outside forces, therefore from outside.
Why is the location not specified?
It was near.
Near to what?
Near to being surrounded.
Láng was also near,
why was Láng specified?
Láng could still be specified.
2.13.2 In the third month,
they buried Xuān Gōng of Wèi.
2.13.3 In summer,
there was a great flood.
2.13.4 In the seventh month of autumn.
2.13.5 In the tenth month of winter.
2.14.1 In the first month of spring in the fourteenth year,
Gōng met with Bó of Zhèng in Cáo.
2.14.2 There was no ice.
Why is it recorded?
To record a strange occurrence.
2.14.3 Summer, the fifth [month].
Bó of Zhèng sent his younger brother Yǔ to come and form an alliance.
What is "summer, the fifth"?
There is nothing to be learned from it.
2.14.4 On rénshēn day of the eighth month in autumn,
the imperial granary caught fire.
What is the imperial granary?
It is where the grains for sacrifice were stored.
Why is the fire in the imperial granary recorded?
To record a disaster.
2.14.5 On yǐhài,
they performed the *cháng* sacrifice.
Ordinary events are not recorded,
so why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is being criticized?
The *cháng* sacrifice is being criticized.
It is saying: Should they still perform the *cháng* sacrifice?
The imperial granary has burned down,
it would be better not to perform the *cháng* sacrifice.
2.14.6 On dīngsì day of the twelfth month of winter,
Lùfù, Hóu of Qí, died.
2.14.7 The people of Sòng, along with the people of Qí, the people of Wèi, the people of Cài, and the people of Chén, attacked Zhèng.
What does "along with" mean?
To carry out their intentions.
2.15.1 In the second month of spring in the fifteenth year,
the King of Heaven sent Jiāfù to request chariots.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is being criticized?
A king should not make requests;
requesting chariots is against propriety.
2.15.2 On yǐwèi day of the third month,
the King of Heaven died.
2.15.3 On jǐsì day of the fourth month in summer,
they buried Xī Gōng of Qí.
2.15.4 In the fifth month,
Bó of Zhèng, Tū, fled to Cài.
Why is he called Tū?
He seized the rightful position.
2.15.5 Hū, the heir apparent of Zhèng, returned to Zhèng.
Why is he called the heir apparent?
He restored the rightful position.
Why do some say "returned" and others say "returned again"?
"Returned again" means that going out was bad, but returning was not bad;
"re-entering" means
that going out was not bad, but entering was bad;
"entering" means
that both going out and entering were bad;
"returning" means
that neither going out nor entering was bad.
2.15.6 Shū of Xǔ entered Xǔ.
2.15.7 Gōng met with Hóu of Qí in Hào.
2.15.8 The people of Zhūlóu, the people of Móu, and the people of Gé came to court.
Why are they all referred to as "people"?
Because they are barbarians.
2.15.9 In the ninth month of autumn,
Bó of Zhèng, Tū, entered Yì.
What is Yì?
It is a city of Zhèng.
Why does it not say "entered Zhèng"?
It is mentioned at the end.
Why is it mentioned at the end?
Jì Zhòng had already fled.
Then why is Hū's flight not mentioned?
Mentioning Hū as the ruler is insignificant;
if Jì Zhòng exists, then he exists;
if Jì Zhòng has fled, then he has fled.
2.15.10 In the eleventh month of winter,
Gōng met with Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, and Hóu of Chén in Chǐ
to attack Zhèng.
2.16.1 In the first month of spring in the sixteenth year,
Gōng met with Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Cài, and Hóu of Wèi in Cáo.
2.16.2 In the fourth month of summer,
Gōng met with Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, Hóu of Chén, and Hóu of Cài to attack Zhèng.
2.16.3 In the seventh month of autumn,
Gōng returned from attacking Zhèng.
2.16.4 In winter,
they fortified Xiàng.
2.16.5 In the eleventh month,
Hóu of Wèi, Shuò, fled to Qí.

If it was against the principles for the feudal lords to exclusively bestow,
then why does it say he substantially bestowed?
Because above there was no Son of Heaven,
and below there was no regional overlord.
When the lords of the land destroyed each other,
if one had the power to rescue,
then it was permissible to rescue.
summer, the sixth month,
*Xíng* moved to *Chényí*.
What does "moved" mean?
It was their intention.
What does "caused to move" mean?
It was not their intention.
The armies of *Qí*, *Sòng*, and *Cáo* fortified *Xíng*.
This is one event,
so why is "armies of *Qí*, *Sòng*, and *Cáo*" repeated?
If "army" were not repeated,
there would be no way to know that it was one event.
autumn, the seventh month, *wùchén*,
Lady *Jiāng* died in *Yí*,
and the people of *Qí* brought her body back.
What is *Yí*?
It is territory of *Qí*.
If it is territory of *Qí*, then why does it say "the people of *Qí* brought her body back"?
If the Lady died in *Yí*,
then the people of *Qí* would bring her body back.
If the Lady died in *Yí*,
then why would the people of *Qí* bring her body back?
*Huán Gōng* summoned her and had her strangled.
The people of *Chǔ* attacked *Zhèng*.
the eighth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of *Qí*, the Duke of *Sòng*, the Count of *Zhèng*, the Count of *Cáo*, and the people of *Zhūlóu* at *Chēng*.
the ninth month,
the Duke defeated the army of *Zhūlóu* at *Yīng*.
winter, the tenth month, *rénwǔ*,
Gongzi *Yǒu* led an army and defeated the army of *Jǔ* at *Lí*,
capturing *Jǔ Ná*.
Who was *Jǔ Ná*?
He was a senior official of *Jǔ*.
*Jǔ* had no senior officials,
so why is this written?
It was because of the capture of the Great *Jìzǐ*.
What was so great about the capture of the Great *Jìzǐ*?
*Jìzǐ*'s management of internal affairs was difficult to correct,
and his defense against external difficulties was difficult to correct.
How was his defense against external difficulties difficult to correct?
When Gongzi *Qìngfù* murdered *Mǐn Gōng*,
he fled to *Jǔ*.
The people of *Jǔ* drove him away,
intending to go through *Qí*.
The people of *Qí* would not admit him,
so he turned back and camped on the banks of the *Wèn* River,
and sent Gongzi *Xīsī* to request entry.
*Jìzǐ* said,
"The Gongzi cannot enter,
if he enters, he will be killed."
*Xīsī* could not bear to report back to *Qìngfù*,
so from the southern bank,
he faced north and wept.
*Qìngfù* heard this and said,
"Alas!
This is the voice of *Xīsī*.
Very well."
He said,
"I cannot enter."
So he hanged himself with the chariot pole.
The people of *Jǔ* heard this and said,
"We have already captured the rebel,
to seek a ransom from *Lǔ*."
The people of *Lǔ* did not give it,
so they raised an army and attacked *Lǔ*.
*Jìzǐ* met them with a partial battle.
the twelfth month, *dīngsì*,
the Lady's funeral procession arrived from *Qí*.
Why isn't the Lady referred to as Lady *Jiāng*?
It is a deprecation.
Why a deprecation?
Because she was involved in the murder of the Duke.
Then why wasn't the deprecation made at the mention of the murder?
A deprecation must be made on the most serious matter,
and nothing is more serious than the arrival of her funeral procession.
5.2.1 In the spring of the second year, the royal first month,
the city of Chǔqiū 楚丘 was walled.
Who walled it?
It was Wèi 衛 that was walled.
Why is it not said "the city of Wèi 衛 was walled"?
Because it was destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
It was probably the Dí 狄 who destroyed it.
Why is it not said "the Dí 狄 destroyed it"?
To conceal it for the sake of Duke Huán 桓公.
Why conceal it for the sake of Duke Huán 桓公?
Because above there was no Son of Heaven (Tiānzǐ 天子),
below there were no regional lords (fāngbó 方伯),
and among the lords of all under Heaven, there were those who destroyed each other.
Duke Huán 桓公 was unable to save them,
so Duke Huán 桓公 was ashamed of it.
Then who walled it?
Duke Huán 桓公 walled it.
Why is it not said "Duke Huán 桓公 walled it"?
Because he did not exclusively bestow fiefs on the lords.
Why did he not bestow?
He actually bestowed, but the text does not say so.
Why does the text not say so?
According to the righteousness of the lords, they should not exclusively bestow fiefs.
According to the righteousness of the lords, they should not exclusively bestow fiefs,
then what does it mean to say "he actually bestowed it"?
Above there was no Son of Heaven (Tiānzǐ 天子),
below there were no regional lords (fāngbó 方伯),
and among the lords of all under Heaven, there were those who destroyed each other.
If he had the power to save them,
then it was permissible to save them.
5.2.2 In the summer, in the fifth month, on the day xīnsì 辛巳,
we buried our lesser ruler, Āijiāng 哀姜.
Who was Āijiāng 哀姜?
She was the wife of Duke Zhuāng 莊公.
The army of Yú 虞 and the army of Jìn 晉 destroyed Xiàyáng 夏陽.
Yú 虞 was a small state.
Why is it placed above the large state?
Because it made Yú 虞 the leader in evil.
Why did it make Yú 虞 the leader in evil?
Yú 虞 accepted bribes
and lent passage to those who destroyed the state
in order to bring about its own ruin.
How did it accept bribes?
Duke Xiàn 獻公 held court with his grand officers and asked them,
saying,
"I, your ruler, last night lay down but could not sleep.
What does this signify?"
Among the grand officers, there was one who came forward and replied,
saying,
"Were you not at ease in your sleep?
Was it perhaps that the attendants were not at your side?"
Duke Xiàn 獻公 did not respond.
Xún Xī 荀息 came forward and said,
"Did you have visions of Yú 虞 and Guō 虢?"
Duke Xiàn 獻公 bowed and invited him forward,
and then went inside with him to discuss the matter, saying,
"I want to attack Guō 虢,
but if I do, Yú 虞 will come to its aid;
if I attack Yú 虞, then Guō 虢 will come to its aid.
What should I do?
I wish to consider this with you."
Xún Xī 荀息 replied,
"If your lordship uses my plan,
then today you will take Guō 虢,
and tomorrow you will take Yú 虞.
What do you have to worry about?"
Duke Xiàn 獻公 said,
"If that is so, then what should I do?"
Xún Xī 荀息 said,
"Please send the chariot of Qūchǎn 屈產
and the white jade of Chuíjí 垂棘 as gifts.
Success is certain.
The treasures will be moved from their inner storage
to the outer treasury;
the horses will be moved from their inner stables
and tied in the outer stables.
What will your lordship lose?"
Duke Xiàn 獻公 said,
"Very well.
However, Gōng Zhīqí 宮之奇 is there.
What should I do?"
Xún Xī 荀息 said,
"Gōng Zhīqí 宮之奇 knows what is going on,
but even so,
Duke Yú 虞 is greedy and loves treasures.
When he sees the treasures,
he will certainly not heed his words.
Please send them anyway."
So he sent them after all.
When Duke Yú 虞 saw the treasures,
he agreed.
Gōng Zhīqí 宮之奇 indeed remonstrated:
"The *Records* say:
'When the lips are gone, the teeth will be cold.'
Yú 虞 and Guō 虢 save each other,
not to give gifts to each other.
If Jìn 晉 takes Guō 虢 today,
then tomorrow Yú 虞 will follow and be destroyed.
Your lordship, please do not agree to it!"
Duke Yú 虞 did not heed his words
and finally lent the road to take Guō 虢.
Four years later,
they turned and took Yú 虞.
Duke Yú 虞 arrived, carrying the treasures and leading the horses.
Xún Xī 荀息 saw him and said,
"How was my plan?"
Duke Xiàn 獻公 said,
"Your plan has already been carried out.
The treasures are my treasures,
but even so,
the teeth of my horses have also grown long."
This was a joke.
What was Xiàyáng 夏陽?
It was the city of Guō 虢.
Why is it not attached to Guō 虢?
It was the state's.
Why was it the state's?
Because the ruler resided there.
5.2.4 In the autumn, in the ninth month,
the Marquis of Qí 齊侯, Duke Sòng 宋公, the men of Jiāng 江, and the men of Huáng 黃 made a covenant at Guànzé 貫澤.
Who were the men of Jiāng 江 and the men of Huáng 黃?
They are referred to as distant states.
When the distant states arrived,
why does China only mention Qí 齊 and Sòng 宋 as having arrived?
The great states are Qí 齊 and Sòng 宋,
the distant states are Jiāng 江 and Huáng 黃,
and the rest are considered to have dared not not arrive.
5.2.5 In the winter, in the tenth month,
there was no rain.
Why is it written?
To record an anomaly.
The men of Chǔ 楚 invaded Zhèng 鄭.
5.3.1 In the spring of the third year, the royal first month,
there was no rain.
In the summer, in the fourth month,
there was no rain.
Why is it written?
To record an anomaly.
The men of Xú 徐 took Shū 舒.
Why does it say "took" it?
Because it was easy.
In the sixth month,
it rained.
Why does it say "in the sixth month it rained"?
Because it rained above, but not much.
In the autumn,
the Marquis of Qí 齊侯, Duke Sòng 宋公, the men of Jiāng 江, and the men of Huáng 黃 met at Yánggǔ 陽穀.
This was a grand meeting.
Why is it mentioned last?
Duke Huán 桓公 said:
"Do not block the valleys,
do not hoard grain,
do not easily change the heir apparent,
do not take a concubine as a wife."
In the winter,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu 公子友 went to Qí 齊 to attend the covenant.
What is "attending the covenant"?
It is going to the other party to covenant.
Why does it say "came to covenant"?
It is coming to us to covenant.
The men of Chǔ 楚 attacked Zhèng 鄭.
5.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year, the royal first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí 齊侯, Duke Sòng 宋公, the Marquis of Chén 陳侯, the Marquis of Wèi 衛侯, the Count of Zhèng 鄭伯, the Viscount of Xǔ 許男, and the Count of Cáo 曹伯 to invade Cài 蔡.
Cài 蔡 collapsed.
What is "collapsed"?
It is those below rebelling against those above.
When it is a state, it is called "collapsed";
when it is a city, it is called "rebelled."
Then they attacked Chǔ 楚
and encamped at Xíng 陘.
Why does it say "encamped at Xíng 陘"?
Because they were waiting.
Who were they waiting for?
They were waiting for Qū Wán 屈完.
5.4.2 In summer, Xǔ Nán Xīnchén died.
5.4.3 The Chǔ general Qū Wán came to take the oath with our army, and the oath was taken at Shàolíng.
Who was Qū Wán?
He was a senior official of Chǔ.
Why was he not referred to as an envoy?
To honor Qū Wán.
Why honor Qū Wán?
Because he was the equivalent of Duke Huán.
What is the meaning of saying the oath was taken with our army and the oath was taken at Shàolíng?
Our army was at Shàolíng.
If the army was at Shàolíng,
then why mention the oath again?
To rejoice that Chǔ submitted.
What is meant by rejoicing that Chǔ submitted?
If Chǔ has a king, it will submit later;
if it does not have a king, it will rebel first.
It is a barbarian tribe
and frequently causes trouble for the Central States.
The southern and northern barbarians collude.
The Central States were almost severed like a thread.
Duke Huán rescued the Central States and repelled the barbarians.
He ultimately pacified Jīng.
Therefore, this was the work of a true king.
What is the significance of saying he "came"?
To recognize Duke Huán as the leader.
If there were events before this and there will be events after this,
then why only in this instance
is Duke Huán recognized as the leader?
To record his achievements.
5.4.4 The people of Qí arrested Chén Yuántāo Tú.
What was the crime of Tāo Tú?
Obstructing the army's path.
How did he obstruct the army's path?
Tāo Tú said to Duke Huán,
"Now that you have subdued the southern barbarians,
why not return with your army along the coast to the east,
subdue the eastern barbarians, and then return?"
Duke Huán said,
"Agreed."
Thereupon, the army returned along the coast to the east
and was greatly trapped in the marshlands of Pèi.
Looking back, they arrested Tāo Tú.
Why is it that in arresting someone, they are sometimes referred to as a *hóu* [marquis] and
sometimes as a person?
Arresting someone referred to as a *hóu* [marquis] is a punitive expedition by the hegemon.
Arresting someone referred to as a person
is not a punitive expedition by the hegemon.
This arrest was for a crime.
Why is it not considered a punitive expedition by the hegemon?
In ancient times, when the Duke of Zhōu campaigned in the east, the western states resented it;
when he campaigned in the west, the eastern states resented it.
Duke Huán asked permission from Chén to pass through their territory in order to attack Chǔ.
The people of Chén did not want him to return through their territory,
because the army's cause was not just.
Instead of rectifying his army, he arrested Tāo Tú.
The punitive expeditions of the ancients
were not like this.
5.4.5 In autumn, the people of Jiāng and the people of Huáng attacked Chén.
5.4.6 In the eighth month, the Duke returned from attacking Chǔ.
Since Chǔ had already submitted, why was it described as an attack?
Because Chǔ had broken the alliance.
5.4.7 The Xǔ Mù Gōng was buried.

5.4.8 In the twelfth month of winter, Gōngsūn Cí led an army to join with the people of Qí, the people of Sòng, the people of Wèi, the people of Zhèng, the people of Xǔ, and the people of Cáo to invade Chén.
5.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring, the Marquis of Jìn killed his heir apparent, Shēnshēng.
Why is it simply said that the Marquis of Jìn killed him?
When an heir apparent or a younger brother by a different mother is killed, referring directly to the ruler indicates the severity of the matter.
5.5.2 Bó Jī of Qǐ came to court to see her son.
What is the meaning of saying she came to court to see her son?
It is an indirect expression,
meaning she came to court together with her son.
5.5.3 In summer, Gōngsūn Cí went to Móu.

5.5.4 The Duke, along with the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Xǔ Nán, and the Earl of Cáo, met with the King's heir apparent at Shǒudài.
Why is this meeting with the King's heir apparent recorded differently?
The heir apparent is noble,
and the heir apparent is still the heir apparent for generations.
5.5.5 In the eighth month of autumn,
the lords took an oath at Shǒudài.
Why are the lords not listed in order?
When a matter is mentioned twice,
the first mention is specific, and the second is general.
The Earl of Zhèng fled and returned without taking the oath.
What is the meaning of saying he fled and returned without taking the oath?
He could not be compelled to take the oath.
If he could not be compelled to take the oath,
then what does it mean to say he fled and returned?
Master Lǔ said,
"It was probably because he did not want to offend the majority with his few."
5.5.6 The people of Chǔ destroyed Xián,
and the Viscount of Xián fled to Huáng.
5.5.7 On the day *wùshēn*, the first day of the ninth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
5.5.8 In winter, the people of Jìn captured the Duke of Yú.
Yú had already been destroyed, so what does it mean to say he was captured?
It means they did not participate in the destruction.
Why did they not participate in the destruction?
"Destruction" is a favorable term for the fall of a state.
"Destruction" refers to when those above and below are of one mind.
5.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring, the royal first month.
5.6.2 In summer, the Duke, along with the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Wèi, and the Earl of Cáo, attacked Zhèng and besieged the New City.
"Besiege" is not said of a city. Why is it said here?
To emphasize the strength of the siege.
5.6.3 In autumn, the people of Chǔ besieged Xǔ, and the lords then rescued Xǔ.
5.6.4 In winter, the Duke returned from attacking Zhèng.
5.7.1 In the seventh year, in spring, the people of Qí attacked Zhèng.
5.7.2 In summer, the Zǐ of Xiǎo Zhūlóu came to court.
5.7.3 Zhèng killed its senior official Shēn Hóu.
Why is the state mentioned in connection with the killing?
Mentioning the state in connection with the killing is language used when a ruler kills a senior official.
5.7.4 In the seventh month of autumn, the Duke, along with the Marquis of Qí, the heir apparent Kuǎn of Chén, and the heir apparent Huá of Zhèng,
took an oath at Níngmǔ.
5.7.5 Earl Bān of Cáo died.
5.7.6 Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Qí.
5.7.7 In winter, the Zhaō Gōng of Cáo was buried.

5.8.1 In the eighth year, in spring, the royal first month, the Duke, along with the King's envoy, the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Xǔ Nán, the Earl of Cáo, the heir apparent Kuǎn of Chén, and the heir apparent Huá of Zhèng,
took an oath at Táo.
Who is the "King's envoy"?
A person of humble status.
Why is he listed above the lords?
Because of the former king's command.
The Earl of Zhèng requested to join the alliance.
What does it mean to request to join the alliance?
To remain in his place and request to participate.
How does he remain in his place and request to participate?
It probably means he contributed to the expenses.
5.8.2 In summer, the Dí attacked Jìn.
In the seventh month of autumn,
they dì at the Tài Miào,
using it to welcome the fūrén.
What is the meaning of "using"?
"Using" means it should not be used.
What is the meaning of "welcoming"?
"Welcoming" means it should not be welcomed.
To dì and welcome the fūrén is
not in accordance with ritual.
Why is the fūrén not referred to as Jiāng shì?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
It is a criticism of taking a concubine as a wife.
How can it be said that she was taken as a wife?
It was likely under duress from the Qí dowry women who arrived first.
In the twelfth month of winter, on dīngwèi,
the Tiān Wáng died.
In the third month of spring, the royal month, on dīngchǒu,
Sòng Gōng Yùshuō died.
Why is the burial not recorded?
It is to avoid mentioning Xiāng Gōng.
In summer,
the Duke met with Zǎi Zhōu Gōng, Qí Hóu, Sòng Zǐ, Wèi Hóu, Zhèng Bó, Xǔ Nán, and Cáo Bó at Kuíqiū.
Who is Zǎi Zhōu Gōng?
He is the one who manages the affairs of the Son of Heaven.
In the seventh month of autumn, on yǐyǒu,
Bó Jī died.
Why is it recorded that she died when she had not yet married?
She was betrothed.
When a woman is betrothed,
she is given a courtesy name and hairpin,
and if she dies, she is mourned as an adult.
In the ninth month, on wùchén,
the lords made a covenant at Kuíqiū.
The covenants of Huán were not recorded by day,
so why is this one recorded by day?
It is a warning.
What is the warning?
At the meeting at Guànzé,
Duke Huán was concerned about the Zhōngguó,
and the Jiāng and Huáng people arrived without being summoned.
At the meeting at Kuíqiū,
Duke Huán was shaken and became arrogant,
and nine states rebelled.
What is the meaning of "shaken"?
It is like saying "trembling."
What is the meaning of "arrogant"?
It is like saying "no one is like me."
On jiǎxū,
Jìn Hóu Guǐzhū died.
In winter,
Lì Kè of Jìn assassinated Xī Qí, the son of his lord.
This was a lord who had not yet ruled for a full year,
so why is it said that he assassinated Xī Qí, the son of his lord?
It is the title for assassinating a lord who has not yet ruled for a full year.
In the first month of spring, the royal month of the tenth year,
the Duke went to Qí.
The Dí destroyed Wēn.
The Viscount of Wēn fled to Wèi.
Lì Kè of Jìn assassinated his lord Zhuō Zi and his grand master Xún Xī.
What is the meaning of "and"?
It means implicated.
There have been many assassinations of lords,
is there no one else implicated besides this?
It is said:
"There were Kǒng Fǔ and Chóu Mù, who were all implicated."
Aside from Kǒng Fǔ and Chóu Mù,
is there no one else implicated?
It is said:
"There is."
If there is, then why is this recorded?
It is because of Xún Xī's virtue.
What is virtuous about Xún Xī?
It can be said that Xún Xī did not go back on his word.
How can it be said that he did not go back on his word?
Xī Qí and Zhuō Zi
were the sons of Lí Jī,
and Xún Xī was their tutor.
Lí Jī was a beauty that could overthrow a nation.
Xiàn Gōng loved her very much
and wanted to establish her son,
so he killed the heir apparent Shēn Shēng.
Shēn Shēng
was tutored by Lì Kè.
When Xiàn Gōng was ill
and about to die,
he said to Xún Xī:
"What must a man do to be considered trustworthy?"
Xún Xī replied:
"If he could make the dead return to life
and the living not be ashamed of his words,
then he could be considered trustworthy."
Xiàn Gōng died,
and Xī Qí was established.
Lì Kè said to Xún Xī:
"The lord killed the rightful heir and established the unrightful,
abandoned the elder and established the younger,
what is to be done?
I wish to discuss it with you."
Xún Xī said:
"The lord once asked me,
and I replied:
'If he could make the dead return to life
and the living not be ashamed of his words,
then he could be considered trustworthy.'"
Lì Kè knew that he could not conspire with him,
so he retreated and assassinated Xī Qí.
Xún Xī established Zhuō Zi,
Lì Kè assassinated Zhuō Zi,
and Xún Xī died for him.
It can be said that Xún Xī did not go back on his word.
In summer,
the Qí Hóu and Xǔ Nán attacked the Northern Róng.
Jìn killed their grand master Lì Kè.
Lì Kè assassinated two lords,
so why is it not said in terms of punishing a traitor?
He was a grand master of Huì Gōng.
Then who established Huì Gōng?
It was Lì Kè.
Lì Kè assassinated Xī Qí and Zhuō Zi
and welcomed Huì Gōng back.
Lì Kè established Huì Gōng,
so why did Huì Gōng kill him?
Huì Gōng said:
"You have already killed those two young fools,
and now you intend to plot against me.
Being a lord for you
wouldn't that be troubling?"
So he killed him.
Then why is Huì Gōng's entry not recorded?
Jìn does not record entries and exits, fearing to name Wén Gōng's faults.
Qí Xiǎobái entered Qí,
so why does it not name Huán Gōng's faults?
Huán Gōng's reign was long,
his virtues were seen throughout the world,
so his original faults were not named.
Wén Gōng's reign was short,
his virtues were not seen throughout the world,
so his original faults were named.
In the seventh month of autumn.
In winter,
there was a great rain of hail.
Why is this recorded?
To record anomalies.
In the spring of the eleventh year,
Jìn killed their grand master Pī Zhèngfǔ.
In summer,
the Duke and his fūrén, Jiāng shì, met with the Qí Hóu at Yánggǔ.
In the eighth month of autumn,
there was a great yǔ sacrifice.
In winter,
the Chǔ people attacked Huáng.
In the third month of spring, the royal month of the twelfth year, on gēngwǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer,
the Chǔ people destroyed Huáng.
In the seventh month of autumn.
In the twelfth month of winter, on dīngchǒu,
Chén Hóu Chùjiù died.
In the spring of the thirteenth year,
the Dí invaded Wèi.
5.13.2 In summer, the fourth month,
the burial of Gōng Xuān (宣公) of Chén (陳) took place.
The duke met with Hóu (侯) of Qí (齊), Gōng (公) of Sòng (宋), Hóu (侯) of Chén (陳), Hóu (侯) of Wèi (衛), Bó (伯) of Zhèng (鄭), Nán (男) of Xǔ (許), and Bó (伯) of Cáo (曹) at Xián (鹹).
In autumn, the ninth month,
there was a great prayer for rain.
In winter,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu (公子友) went to Qí (齊).
In the fourteenth year, in spring,
the lords walled Yuánlíng (緣陵).
Who walled it?
It was walled by Qǐ (杞).
Why was Qǐ (杞) walled?
It was extinguished.

"Returned him to (歸之于)" means

"Returned to (歸于)" means

Wéngōng (文公) expelled the Hóu of Wèi (衛侯) and installed Shū Wǔ (叔武),

Wéngōng (文公) caused it.
