Chéng Fēng is honorable.
The burial of Cáo Gòng Gōng.
6.10.1 In the third month of the tenth year, in the spring, on *xīnmǎo*,
Zāngsūn Chén died.
6.10.2 In summer,
Qín attacked Jìn.
6.10.3 Chǔ killed their high official Yí Shēn.
6.10.4 From the first month it did not rain,
until the seventh month of autumn.
6.10.5 And Sū Zǐ made a covenant at Nǚlì.
6.10.6 In winter,
the Dí invaded Sòng.
6.10.7 Chǔ Zǐ and the Marquis of Cài were stationed at Qū Hè.
6.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring,
Chǔ Zǐ attacked Juān.
6.11.2 In summer,
Shū Pēngshēng met with Xì Quē of Jìn at Chéngkuāng.
6.11.3 In autumn,
the Earl of Cáo came to court.
6.11.4 Gōngzǐ Suì went to Sòng.
6.11.5 The Dí invaded Qí.
6.11.6 In the tenth month of winter, on *jiǎwǔ*,
Shūsūn Déchén defeated the Dí at Xián.
Who are the Dí?
The long Dí.
There were three brothers,
one went to Qí,
one went to Lǔ,
and one went to Jìn.
The one who went to Qí,
Wángzǐ Chéngfù killed him.
The one who went to Lǔ,
Shūsūn Déchén killed him.
Then we do not know what happened to the one who went to Jìn.
What is meant by "defeated"?
To magnify it.
What about the day?
To magnify it.
What about the place?
To magnify it.
Why is it recorded?
To record anomalies.
6.12.1 In the twelfth year, in the first month of spring,
Shèng Bó came to seek refuge.
Who is Shèng Bó?
A ruler who lost his territory.
Why is he not named?
It is a humble reference to his brothers.
6.12.2 The Earl of Qǐ came to court.
6.12.3 On *gēngzǐ* in the second month,
Zǐ Shūjī died.
Why is "died" used for someone who has not yet married?
She was betrothed.
When a woman is betrothed,
she is given a courtesy name and a hairpin,
and upon death, she is treated with the funeral rites of an adult.
Why is she referred to as *zǐ*?
It is a mark of nobility.
How is she noble?
She is a younger sister of the mother.
6.12.4 In summer,
the Chǔ people besieged Cháo.
6.12.5 In autumn,
the Viscount of Téng came to court.
6.12.6 The Bó of Qín sent Suì to come and present gifts.
Who was Suì?
A senior official of Qín.
Qín had no senior officials;
why is this written?
It praises Mù Gōng.
What is praiseworthy about Mù Gōng?
It considers him capable of change.
How was he capable of change?
Only those who are glib are good at clever speech.
They cause gentlemen to easily become lax.
Moreover, how much more so those who possess many such qualities?
Only someone who is resolute and upright,
without other skills,
whose heart is generous
and capable of tolerance—
this is difficult.
6.12.7 In the twelfth month of winter, on the day wùwǔ, the men of Jìn and the men of Qín fought at Héqu.
This was a partial battle.
Why is it not said that the army suffered a rout?
They were evenly matched.
Why use the term "water land"?
Héqu was sparsely populated;
the Hé River has one bend every thousand *lǐ*.
Jìsūn Hángfǔ led an army to fortify Zhūji and Yùn.
6.13.1 In the thirteenth year, spring, the king's first month.
6.13.2 In the fifth month of summer, on the day rénwǔ, Hóu Shuò of Chén died.
6.13.3 Zūlóu Zǐ Qúchú died.
6.13.4 From the first month it did not rain until the seventh month of autumn.
6.13.5 The house of the ancestral shrine collapsed.
What is the ancestral shrine?
The temple of the Gōng of Lǔ.
The Duke of Zhōu is referred to as the Great Temple;
the Gōng of Lǔ is referred to as the Ancestral Shrine;
the various dukes are referred to as palaces.
This is the temple of the Gōng of Lǔ.
Why is it called the Ancestral Shrine?
The Ancestral Shrine is like an ancestral shrine;
it is not destroyed for generations.
Why is the Duke of Zhōu called the Great Temple in Lǔ?
He enfeoffed the Gōng of Lǔ as the Duke of Zhōu.
The Duke of Zhōu bows in front;
the Gōng of Lǔ bows behind.
It says:
"In life, use it to nourish the Duke of Zhōu;
in death, use it to serve as the host for the Duke of Zhōu."
In that case, did the Duke of Zhōu go to Lǔ?
It says: "He did not go to Lǔ.
He enfeoffed the Gōng of Lǔ as the Duke of Zhōu."
In that case, why did the Duke of Zhōu not go to Lǔ?
He wished for the world to be unified through the Duke of Zhōu.
What did Lǔ use as sacrificial animals when sacrificing to the Duke of Zhōu?
The Duke of Zhōu used a white bull;
the Gōng of Lǔ used a red bull.
The various dukes did not use any (毛 *máo* - fur/hair - used as euphemism for blood sacrifices).
What did Lǔ use as containers when sacrificing to the Duke of Zhōu?
The Duke of Zhōu used *shèng*;
the Gōng of Lǔ used *dào*;
the various dukes used *lǐn*.
Why is it written that the house of the ancestral shrine collapsed?
To criticize.
What is being criticized?
That it had not been repaired for a long time.
6.13.6 In winter,
the Gōng went to Jìn.
6.13.7 The Hóu of Wèi met at Tà.
6.13.8 The Dí invaded Wèi.
6.13.9 In the twelfth month, on the day jǐchǒu,
the Gōng and the Hóu of Jìn made a covenant.
6.13.10 He returned from Jìn.
6.13.11 The Bó of Zhèng met the Gōng at Fěi.
What is meant by "returned"?
It is a well-chosen word.
Why is it well-chosen?
Going, he sided with (Jìn).
The Hóu of Wèi met the Gōng at Tà,
until he was able to make a covenant with the Hóu of Jìn.
Returning, he sided with (Zhèng).
The Bó of Zhèng met the Gōng at Fěi,
therefore, it is praised.
6.14.1 In the fourteenth year, spring, the king's first month,
the Gōng arrived from Jìn.
6.14.2 The people of Zūlóu attacked our southern borders.
6.14.3 Shū Péngshēng led an army to attack Zūlóu.
6.14.4 In the fifth month of summer, on the day yǐhài,
Hóu Pān of Qí died.
6.14.5 In the sixth month,
the Gōng met with Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Chén, Hóu of Wèi, Bó of Zhèng, Xǔ Nán, Cáo Bó, and Zhào Dùn of Jìn.
On the day guǐyǒu,
they formed an alliance at Xīnchéng.
6.14.6 In the seventh month of autumn,
a comet entered the Northern Dipper.
What is a *bèi*?
A comet.
Why does it say it entered the Northern Dipper?
The Northern Dipper has a center.
Why is it written?
To record a strange event.
6.14.7 The Gōng arrived from the meeting.
6.14.8 The men of Jìn tried to install Jiē Zī in Zūlóu,
but were unable to install him.
What is meant by "install"?
It is a way of saying "enter."
Why does it say they were unable to install him?
It magnifies their inability to install him.
What is magnified about their inability to install him?
Xì Quē of Jìn led an army with eight hundred chariots to install Jiē Zī in Zūlóu,
and their strength was so abundant that they could have installed him with ease.
The people of Zūlóu said:
"Jiē Zī is produced by Jìn,
and Qū Qiě is produced by Qí.
If you count using your fingers,
then there are four Jiē Zī,
and six Qū Qiě.
If you use a great state to pressure us,
then it is not known whether Qí or Jìn has them.
If we value them, then we value them both.
However,
Qū Qiě is older."
Xì Quē said:
"It is not that my strength is insufficient to install him,
but righteousness truly does not allow me to do so."
He led his army away,
therefore, gentlemen magnify his inability to install him.
This is Xì Quē of Jìn;
why does it refer to him as "a person"?
To demean him.
Why demean him?
Because he did not allow a senior official to exclusively depose or install a ruler.
Why did he not allow it?
In reality, he allowed it, but not in writing.
Why not in writing?
The righteousness of a senior official does not allow him to exclusively depose or install a ruler.
6.14.9 In the ninth month, on the day jiǎshēn,
Gōngsūn Áo died in Qí.
6.14.10 Gōngzǐ Shāngrén of Qí murdered his ruler, Shě.
This was a ruler who had not yet completed a year;
why does it say he murdered his ruler, Shě?
He had installed him himself,
and he killed him himself,
thereby completing the death of the former and demeaning the life of the latter.
6.14.11 Sòng Zǐ Āi came to seek refuge.
Who was Sòng Zǐ Āi?
He is unheard of.
6.14.12 In winter,
Dān Bó went to Qí;
the people of Qí arrested Dān Bó;
the people of Qí arrested Zǐ Shū Jī.
Why are some arrests referred to as "travelers"
and others not referred to as "travelers"?
Those who are referred to as "travelers" and then arrested
are arrested because of their mission.
Those who are not referred to as "travelers" and then arrested
are arrested for their own sake.
What was Dān Bó's crime?
Immorality in the Way.
Where was he immoral?
He was immoral with Zǐ Shū Jī.
In that case, why does it not say "the people of Qí arrested Dān Bó and Zǐ Shū Jī"?
It is an internal term,
making it seem as if they were different crimes.
6.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Jìn.
In the third month,
Sòng Sīmǎ Huásūn came to form an alliance.
In summer,
the Bó of Cáo came to court.
6.15.4 The people of Qí returned the funeral of Gōngsūn Áo.
Why is "came" not mentioned?
It is a deprecatory expression.
Being coerced to return it to me,
it was like Sǔn Jiàng came here.
On the first day (shuò) of the sixth month, Xīncǒu, there was a solar eclipse.
They used drums and a sacrificial animal at the Shè altar.
6.15.6 Dān Bó arrived from Qí.
Xì Quē of Jìn led an army to attack Cài.
On Wùshēn,
they entered Cài.
Entering, it doesn't mention attacking,
why does this mention attacking?
It was the day they arrived.
What day was it?
It was the day they arrived.
6.15.8 In autumn,
the people of Qí invaded our western border.
Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Jìn.
In the eleventh month of winter,
the lords allied at Hù.
6.15.11 In the twelfth month,
the people of Qí came to return Zishū Jī.
Why does it say "came"?
It was out of compassion for her.
She committed a crime,
why have compassion?
Parents towards their children,
even if they have committed a crime,
still seem to not want them to admit guilt.
6.15.12 The Hóu of Qí invaded our western border,
then attacked Cáo,
entering its outer wall (fú).
What is fú?
It is a broad outer wall.
Is entering the outer wall recorded?
It says it is not recorded.
Entering the outer wall is not recorded,
why is this recorded?
It disturbed us.
What is meant by "disturbed us"?
It is a deprecatory expression.
In reality, we were disturbed by it.
6.16.1 In the spring of the sixteenth year,
Jìsūn Hángfǔ met with the Hóu of Qí at Yánggǔ,
but the Hóu of Qí did not complete the alliance.
Why does it say "did not complete the alliance"?
He was not seen in the alliance.
In the fifth month of summer,
the Duke did not observe the first day (shuò) four times.
Why did the Duke not observe the first day four times?
The Duke was ill.
Why say that the Duke was ill and did not observe the first day?
From then on, the Duke did not observe the first day even when not ill.
Then why not say that the Duke did not observe the first day when not ill?
Having an illness can still be mentioned,
not having an illness cannot be mentioned.
6.16.3 On the day Wùchén of the sixth month,
Gōngzǐ Suì and the Hóu of Qí formed an alliance at Xīqiū.
In the eighth month of autumn, on Xīnwèi, Fūrén Jiāngshì passed away.
The Quántái was destroyed.
What is Quántái?
It is the Lángtái.
If it is the Lángtái, then why is it called Quántái?
Before it was completed it was the Lángtái,
after it was completed it was the Quántái.
Why is destroying the Quántái recorded?
It is criticized.
What is being criticized?
Building it is criticized,
destroying it is criticized.
The ancestors built it,
and he destroyed it himself,
it would have been better to not live there at all.
6.16.6 The people of Chǔ, the people of Qín, and the people of Bā destroyed Yōng.
In the eleventh month of winter,
the people of Sòng assassinated their lord Chùjiù.
Why do some assassins of lords have their names mentioned?
And some do not have their names mentioned?
If a high official (dàfū) assassinates the lord, their name is mentioned,
and those of low status are treated as common criminals.
If high officials kill each other, they are referred to as "people",
and those of low status are treated as robbers.
6.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
the people of Jìn, the people of Wèi, the people of Chén, and the people of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
On Guǐhài in the fourth month of summer,
we buried our minor consort Shèng Jiāng.
Who is Shèng Jiāng?
She is the mother of Duke Wén.
6.17.3 The Hóu of Qí attacked our western border.
On Guǐwèi in the sixth month,
the Duke and the Hóu of Qí formed an alliance at Gǔ.
The lords gathered at Hù.
6.17.6 In autumn,
the Duke arrived from Gǔ.
In winter,
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí.
In the second month of the eighteenth year, the royal spring, on Dīngchǒu,
the Duke passed away beneath the terrace.
6.18.2 The Bó of Qín, Yīng, passed away.
On Wùxū in the fifth month of summer,
the people of Qí assassinated their lord Shāngrén.
On Guǐyǒu in the sixth month,
we buried our lord, Duke Wén.
6.18.5 In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Suì and Shūsūn Déchén went to Qí.
In the tenth month of winter,
Zǐ passed away.
Who is referred to as "Zǐ passed away"?
It refers to Zǐ Chì.
Why is the day not mentioned?
It is concealed.
Why concealed?
It was an assassination.
If it was an assassination, why is the day not mentioned?
They could not bear to say it.
6.18.7 Fūrén Jiāngshì returned to Qí.
Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Qí.
Jǔ assassinated its lord Shùqí.
Why is the state mentioned in the assassination?
Mentioning the state in the assassination is
a way of saying that the masses assassinated the lord.
7.1.1 In the first year, the royal first month of spring,
the Duke ascended to the throne.
Successions following assassinations of lords do not mention "ascended to the throne,"
why is "ascended to the throne" mentioned here?
It was according to his wishes.
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí to welcome the bride.
In the third month,
the duke then brought fūrén Fù Jiāng from Qí.
Why is "gōngzǐ Suí" not used?
A matter seen twice
is the final name.
Why is "fūrén" not called Jiāng Shì?
It is a demotion.
Why demotion?
To criticize marrying during mourning.
If marrying during mourning concerned the duke,
then why demote the fūrén?
There is no way to demote the duke internally.
If there is no way to demote the duke internally,
then why demote the fūrén?
The fūrén and the duke are one body.
Why is she called "fù"?
It is a term used when there is a mother-in-law.
In summer,
Jìsūn Xíngfǔ went to Qí.
Jìn exiled its grand master Xū Jiǎfù to Wèi.
What does "exiled" mean?
It means "no departure," that is all.
Then why say it?
To be close to correctness.
How is this close to correctness?
In ancient times, after a grand master had left,
he waited to be exiled for three years.
If the lord exiled him, it was wrong;
if the grand master waited to be exiled, it was correct.
In ancient times, if a minister had a major bereavement,
the lord would not call at his door for three years.
Once the *liàn* ceremony was complete,
he could wear the cap and gown
and perform military duties.
If the lord ordered him to do so, it was wrong;
if the minister carried it out, it was proper,
as Mǐn Zǐ insisted on wearing mourning garb while performing his duties.
Afterward, he said:
"If this is the ancient way,
it does not accord with people's feelings."
He resigned and retired.
Kǒngzǐ probably approved of this.
The duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Píngzhōu.
Gōngzǐ Suí went to Qí.
In the sixth month,
the people of Qí seized the fields west of the Jì River.
Seizing an outer city is not recorded,
so why is this recorded?
It was to bribe Qí.
Why bribe Qí?
It was the bribe for killing Zǐ Chì.
In autumn,
the ruler of Zhūlóu came to court.
The Viscount of Chǔ and the people of Zhèng invaded Chén,
and then invaded Sòng.
Zhào Dùn of Jìn led an army to rescue Chén.
The Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Wèi, and the Count of Cáo met the Jìn army at Fěilín
to attack Zhèng.
This was the army of Zhào Dùn of Jìn.
Why is it not said to be the army of Zhào Dùn?
It is the way of saying that lords do not meet with grand masters.
In winter,
Zhào Chuān of Jìn led an army to invade Liǔ.
What is Liǔ?
It is a city of the Son of Heaven.
Why is it not connected to Zhōu?
It is not participating in attacking the Son of Heaven.
The people of Jìn and the people of Sòng attacked Zhèng.
In the second year, spring, the royal second month, *rénzǐ*,
Huá Yuán of Sòng led an army and Gōngzǐ Guīshēng of Zhèng led an army to fight at Dàjí;
the Sòng army was defeated,
and Huá Yuán of Sòng was captured.
The Qín army attacked Jìn.
In summer,
the people of Jìn, the people of Sòng, the people of Wèi, and the people of Chén invaded Zhèng.
In autumn, the ninth month, *yǐchǒu*,
Zhào Dùn of Jìn assassinated his lord, Yí Háo.
In winter, the tenth month, *yǐhài*,
the Heavenly King died.
In the third year, spring, the royal first month,
the suburban ox was injured in the mouth;
they changed and divined for an ox;
the ox died;
therefore, they did not perform the suburban sacrifice,
but still presented the offerings three times.
What does this say?
It was a delay.
Why not divine again?
Nurturing sacrificial animals involves nurturing two.
If the divination for the imperial sacrificial animal is not auspicious,
then rely on the millet sacrificial animal and divine with it.
The imperial sacrificial animal is purified for three months,
while for the millet animal, only preparations are watched.
Then why necessarily sacrifice to the God of Millet in the suburban sacrifice?
Kings must match with their ancestor.
Then why must kings match with their ancestor?
What comes from within cannot proceed without a mate;
what comes from outside cannot stop without a host.
The burial of King Kuāng.
The Viscount of Chǔ attacked the Bēn Hún Róng.
In summer,
the people of Chǔ invaded Zhèng.
In autumn,
the Chì Dí invaded Qí.
The Sòng army besieged Cáo.
In winter, the tenth month, *bǐngxū*,
Bólán of Zhèng died.
The burial of Duke Mù of Zhèng.
In the fourth year, spring, the royal first month,
the duke and the Marquis of Qí made peace between Jǔ and Tán.
The people of Jǔ were unwilling;
the duke attacked Jǔ
and seized Xiàng.
This was making peace with Jǔ;
why does it say "were unwilling"?
It excuses the seizure of Xiàng.
Earl Dào of Qín died.
In summer, the sixth month, *yǐyǒu*,
Gōngzǐ Guīshēng of Zhèng assassinated his lord, Yí.
The Chì Dí invaded Qí.
In autumn,
the duke went to Qí.
The duke returned from Qí.
In winter,
the Viscount of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
In the fifth year, spring,
the duke went to Qí.
In summer,
the duke returned from Qí.
In autumn, the ninth month,
Gāo Gù of Qí came to meet Zǐ Shū Jī.
Shūsūn Déchén died.
In winter,
Gāo Gù of Qí and Zǐ Shū Jī came;
why mention the coming of Gāo Gù?
If the coming of Shū Jī is mentioned, but not the coming of Gāo Gù, it would be impermissible.
Zǐ Gōngyáng Zǐ said:
"Is it perhaps because they came together as a pair?"
The people of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
In the spring of the sixth year,
Jìn’s Zhào Dùn and Wèi’s Sūn Miǎn invaded Chén.
Zhào Dùn assassinated the ruler;
how is this reflected again here?
The one who personally assassinated the ruler was Zhào Chuān.
The one who personally assassinated the ruler was Zhào Chuān,
then why is it attributed to Zhào Dùn?
He did not punish the traitor.
How can it be said that he did not punish the traitor?
The historian of Jìn wrote about the traitor, saying:
"Jìn’s Zhào Dùn assassinated his ruler Yí Háo."
Zhào Dùn said:
"Heaven, I am innocent!
I did not assassinate the ruler;
who says that I assassinated the ruler?"
The historian said:
"You act with benevolence and righteousness;
someone assassinated your ruler,
and upon returning to the state, you did not punish the traitor.
How is this not assassinating the ruler?"
How did Zhào Dùn return to the state?
Líng Gōng was without principle,
making all the high officials enter the inner court,
and then stationing himself on the terrace,
drawing a pellet bow and shooting at them.
They would rush to avoid the pellets;
this was his only amusement.
Zhào Dùn had already attended court and was leaving,
standing with the high officials in the court,
when someone carrying a dirt basket
came out from the inner chamber.
Zhào Dùn said:
"What is that?
Why is a dirt basket coming out from the inner chamber?"
Calling him, he did not come;
he said:
"You are a high official;
if you want to see it, then go and see it."
Zhào Dùn went and saw it,
and it was a ghastly dead man.
Zhào Dùn said:
"What is this?"
He said:
"It is the cook;
the bear paws were not well-cooked,
the Duke was angry,
and killed him with a dipper,
dismembered him,
and ordered me to discard him."
Zhào Dùn said:
"Alas!"
He rushed in.
Líng Gōng saw Zhào Dùn and was fearful, bowing twice.
Zhào Dùn hesitated, faced north, bowed twice, and kowtowed,
rushing out.
Líng Gōng felt ashamed
and wanted to kill him.
Thereupon he sent a certain brave warrior to kill him.
The brave warrior entered his main gate,
but there was no one guarding the gate;
entering his inner chamber,
there was no one guarding the inner chamber;
going up to his hall,
there was no one there.
Looking down and peering into his door,
he was eating a simple meal of fish and rice.
The brave warrior said:
"Alas!
You are truly a benevolent man!
I entered your main gate,
but there was no one there;
entering your inner chamber,
there was no one there;
going up to your hall,
there was no one there;
this shows your unguardedness.
You are an important minister of the state of Jìn, yet you eat a simple meal of fish and rice;
this shows your frugality.
The ruler wants to send me to kill you,
but I cannot bear to kill you.
However,
I also cannot face my ruler again."
Then he cut his own throat and died.
Líng Gōng heard of this
and was angry.
He desired even more to kill him,
but there was no one he could send.
Thereupon he laid an ambush in the palace
and summoned Zhào Dùn to dine with him.
Zhào Dùn’s charioteer, Qí Mí Míng,
was the strongest man in the state.
Sturdily he followed Zhào Dùn and entered,
placing his weapon below the hall and standing there.
Zhào Dùn had finished eating,
and Líng Gōng said to Dùn:
"I have heard that your sword is a sharp sword;
show it to me;
I want to see it."
Zhào Dùn rose
and was about to present the sword,
when Qí Mí Míng called to him from below, saying:
"Dùn, when you have finished eating, leave;
why are you drawing your sword in the ruler's presence?"
Zhào Dùn knew the situation,
hesitated at the steps, and ran.
Líng Gōng had a Zhōu dog,
called Áo,
and calling Áo, he set it after him.
Áo also hesitated at the steps and followed him.
Qí Mí Míng went against it and tripped it,
severing its throat.
Zhào Dùn looked back and said:
"Your ruler's dog is not as good as my charioteer!"
Then armored soldiers in the palace beat their drums and rose up,
and one who rose from among the armored soldiers embraced Zhào Dùn and mounted him.
Zhào Dùn looked back and said:
"How did I obtain this from you?"
He said:
"You once saved my life under a mulberry tree."
Zhào Dùn said:
"What is your name?"
He said:
"For whom does my ruler act as an attendant?

The Hùo was moved.
Jìsūn Sù went to Jìn.
The funeral of Cáo Chéng Gōng.
Summer,
Wèi Sūn Línfù led troops to attack Qí.
Autumn, seventh month, Xīnmǎo,
Hóu Yuán of Qí died.
Shì Gài of Jìn led troops to invade Qí,
reaching Gǔ,
hearing of the death of the Lord of Qí,
then returned.
Why did he return?
A good excuse.
What good is it?
Magnifying that he did not attack during mourning.
If he received the order from the ruler to attack Qí,
then why magnify that he did not attack during mourning?
The grandee went out on the ruler's command,
advance and retreat are up to the grandee.
Eighth month, Bǐngchén,
Zhòngsūn Miè died.
Qí killed its grandee Gāo Hòu.
Zhèng killed its grandee Gōngzǐ Xǐ.
Winter,
the funeral of Líng Gōng of Qí.
The outer city wall was built on the west.
Shūsūn Bào met with Shì Gài of Jìn at Kē.
The city of Wǔchéng was built.
In the twentieth year, spring, the king's first month, Xīnhài,
Zhòngsūn Sù met with the Jǔ people,
making a covenant at Xiàng.
Summer, sixth month, Gēngshēn,
the Duke met with Hóu of Jìn, Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, Bó of Zhèng, Bó of Cáo, Zǐ of Jǔ, Zū Lóu Zǐ, Zǐ of Téng, Bó of Xuē, Bó of Qǐ, and Xiǎo Zū Lóu Zǐ,
making a covenant at Chányuān.
Autumn,
the Duke arrived from the meeting.
Zhòngsūn Sù led troops to attack Zū Lóu.
Cài killed its grandee Gōngzǐ Xiè.
Gōngzǐ Lǚ of Cài fled to Chǔ.
Guāng, the younger brother of the Lord of Chén, fled to Chǔ.
Shū Lǎo went to Qí.
Winter, tenth month, Bǐngchén, first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Jìsūn Sù went to Sòng.
In the twenty-first year, spring, the king's first month,
the Duke went to Jìn.
Shùqí of Zū Lóu came to seek refuge with lacquer and Lǘqiū.
Who was Shùqí of Zū Lóu?
A grandee of Zū Lóu.
Zū Lóu had no grandees,
why is this recorded?
Because of the importance of the land.
Summer,
the Duke arrived from Jìn.
Autumn,
Luán Yíng of Jìn fled to Chǔ.
Ninth month, Gēngxū, first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Winter, tenth month, Gēngchén, first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Bó of Cáo came to court.
The Duke met with Hóu of Jìn, Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, Bó of Zhèng, Bó of Cáo, Zǐ of Jǔ, and Zū Lóu Zǐ at Shāngrèn.
Eleventh month, Gēngzǐ,
Kǒngzǐ was born.
In the twenty-second year, spring, the king's first month,
the Duke arrived from the meeting.
Fourth month of summer.
Autumn, seventh month, Xīnyǒu,
Shū Lǎo died.
Winter,
the Duke met with Hóu of Jìn, Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, Bó of Zhèng, Bó of Cáo, Zǐ of Jǔ, Zū Lóu Zǐ, Zǐ of Téng, Bó of Xuē, Bó of Qǐ, and Xiǎo Zū Lóu Zǐ at Shāsuí.
The Duke arrived from the meeting.
Chǔ killed its grandee Gōngzǐ Zhuīshū.
In the twenty-third year, spring, second month of the king, Guǐyǒu, first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Third month, Jǐsì,
Bó Gài of Qǐ died.
Summer,
Bíwǒ of Zū Lóu came to seek refuge.
Who was Bíwǒ of Zū Lóu?
A grandee of Zū Lóu.
Zū Lóu had no grandees,
why is this recorded?
Because he was close.
The funeral of Xiào Gōng of Qǐ.
Chén killed its grandees Qìng Hǔ and Qìng Yín.
Guāng, the younger brother of the Lord of Chén, returned to Chén from Chǔ.
Luán Yíng of Jìn re-entered Jìn,
entering at Qūwò.
What was Qūwò?
A city of Jìn.
Why does it say "entered Jìn" and "entered Qūwò"?
Luán Yíng was about to enter Jìn,
but the Jìn people did not allow him in,
so he entered through Qūwò.
Autumn,
the Lord of Qí attacked Wèi,
then attacked Jìn.
Eighth month,
Shūsūn Bào led troops to rescue Jìn,
stationing himself at Yōngyú.
Why is "rescue" mentioned first and then "stationing"?
To communicate the ruler's command first.
Jǐmǎo,
Zhòngsūn Sù died.
Winter, tenth month, Yǐhài,
Zāngsūn Hé fled to Zū Lóu.
The Jìn people killed Luán Yíng.
Why does it not say "killed their grandee"?
He was not their grandee.
The Lord of Qí ambushed Jǔ.
In the twenty-fourth year, spring,
Shūsūn Bào went to Jìn.
9.24.2 Zhòngsūn Jié led troops to invade Qí.
9.24.3 In summer,
the Chǔzǐ attacked Wú.
In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, jiǎzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse that
was total.
Qí's Cuī Zhù led troops to attack Jǔ.
There was a great flood.
On the first day of the eighth month, guǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.

The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, the Viscount of Jǔ, the Viscount of Zhūlóu, the Viscount of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, and the Viscount of Xiǎozhūlóu at Chényí.
In winter,
the Chǔzǐ, the Marquis of Cài, the Marquis of Chén, and the Viscount of Xǔ attacked Zhèng.
The Duke returned from the meeting.
Chén Zhēn Yíjiù fled to Chǔ.
Shūsūn Bào went to the capital.
There was a great famine.
In the spring of the twenty-fifth year,
Qí's Cuī Zhù led troops to attack our northern borderlands.
In summer, on the yǐhài day of the fifth month,
Qí's Cuī Zhù murdered his lord, Guāng.

The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, the Viscount of Jǔ, the Viscount of Zhūlóu, the Viscount of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, and the Viscount of Xiǎozhūlóu at Chényí.
On the rénzǐ day of the sixth month,
Zhèng's Gōngsūn Shèzhī led troops to enter Chén.
In autumn, on the jǐsì day of the eighth month,
the lords formed an alliance at Chóngqiū.
The Duke returned from the meeting.
The Marquis of Wèi entered Chényí.
What is Chényí?
It is a city of Wèi.
Why does it not say he entered Wèi?
It is to condemn the lord for being murdered.
Chǔ's Qū Jiàn led troops and extinguished Shūjiū.
In winter,
Zhèng's Gōngsūn Chài led troops to attack Chén.
In the twelfth month,
the Wú Zǐ Yè attacked Chǔ,
and was stopped at Cháo,
and died.
What does it mean that he was stopped at Cháo and died?
It means he entered the gates of Cháo and died.
What does it mean that he entered the gates of Cháo and died?
It means he entered the gates of Cháo and then died.
Why is the Wú Zǐ Yè named thus?
He was wounded and turned back,
but did not reach his lodging before he died.
In the spring, the royal second month, xīn mǎo day, of the twenty-sixth year,
Wèi's Níng Xǐ murdered his lord, Piāo.
Wèi's Sūn Línfǔ entered Qī in rebellion.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
the Marquis of Wèi, Kàn, returned to Wèi.
This condemns the lord for being murdered.
Why does it say he returned?
It is to show contempt for Piāo.
Why show contempt for Piāo?
There was no explanation for Piāo's establishment.
In that case, why not say that Piāo was established?
The reason for not saying that Piāo was established
is to show contempt for the Marquis of Wèi.
In summer,
the Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Wú to come on a diplomatic visit.
The Duke met with the people of Jìn, Zhèng Liángxiāo, the people of Sòng, and the people of Cáo at Chányuān.
In autumn,
the Duke of Sòng killed his heir apparent, Cuó.
The people of Jìn captured Wèi's Níng Xǐ.
This was capturing someone guilty,
so why is it not considered a punitive expedition by the hegemon?
It was not capturing him for his crime.
On the rénwǔ day of the eighth month,
the Viscount of Xǔ, Níng, died in Chǔ.
In winter,
the Chǔzǐ, the Marquis of Cài, and the Marquis of Chén attacked Zhèng.
The Ling Duke of Xǔ was buried.
In the spring of the twenty-seventh year,
the Marquis of Qí sent Qìng Fēng to come on a diplomatic visit.
In summer,
Shūsūn Bào met with Jìn's Zhào Wǔ, Chǔ's Qū Jiàn, Cài's Gōngsūn Guīshēng, Wèi's Shí È, Chén's Kǒng Yuán, Zhèng's Liángxiāo, the people of Xǔ, and the people of Cáo in Sòng.
Wèi killed its grand master, Níng Xǐ,
and the Marquis of Wèi's younger brother, Zhuān, fled to Jìn.
Wèi killed its grand master, Níng Xǐ,
so why did the Marquis of Wèi's younger brother, Zhuān, flee to Jìn?
He fled because of the killing of Níng Xǐ.
Why did he flee because of the killing of Níng Xǐ?
Wèi Níng Zhí and Sūn Línfǔ drove out the Marquis of Wèi and established Gōngsūn Piāo.
Níng Zhí was sick and about to die,
and said to Xǐ:
"It was not my intention to depose the duke,
it was the Sūn clan who did it.
If I die,
can you be sure to restore the duke?"
Xǐ said:
"Yes."
Níng Zhí died,
and Xǐ was established as a grand master.
He sent someone to say to Duke Xiàn:
"It was not the Níng clan who deposed the duke,
it was the Sūn clan who did it.
What do you think about my wanting to restore the duke?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"If you are willing to restore me,
I ask to make a covenant with you."
Xǐ said:
"There is no need to make a covenant,
please have Gongzi Zhuān negotiate it."
Duke Xiàn said to Gongzi Zhuān:
"The Níng clan is going to restore me,
and I want to make a covenant with them.
But they say:
'There is no need to make a covenant,
please have Gongzi Zhuān negotiate it.'
You must negotiate it for me."
Gongzi Zhuān declined, saying:
"To carry the bridle and reins,
and hold the axe and chisel to follow the lord east, west, north, and south,
these are the affairs of servants and concubines' sons.
But as for establishing trust through covenants,
this is not something that servants and concubines' sons dare to participate in."
Duke Xiàn angrily said:
"The ones who deposed me
were not only the Níng clan and the Sūn clan,
but all of you!"
Gongzi Zhuān had no choice but to negotiate with him.
After negotiating,
he returned
and arrived,
and killed Níng Xǐ.
Gongzi Zhuān took his wife and children and left,
intending to cross the river,
he held his wife and children and made a covenant with them,
saying:
"If anyone sets foot on Wèi land
or eats Wèi grain,
may the pheasant deceive them."
In autumn, on the xīnsì day of the seventh month,
Bào and the grand masters of the lords formed an alliance in Sòng.
Why is Bào mentioned again?
It is a criticism of the lords.
Why is it a criticism of the lords?
It is because Wèi's Shí È was there,
saying that the followers of evil people were there.
In winter, on the yǐhài day, the first day of the twelfth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the spring of the twenty-eighth year,
there was no ice.
In summer,
Wèi's Shí È fled to Jìn.
The Viscount of Zhūlóu came to court.
9.28.4 In the eighth month of autumn,
there was a great rainmaking ceremony.
Zhòngsūn Jié went to Jìn.
9.28.5 In winter,
Qìng Fēng of Qí came to seek refuge.

the Duke went to Chǔ.

the Heavenly King died.
9.28.8 On the Jǐwèi day,
Chǔ Zǐ Zhāo died.
9.29.1 In the first month of spring, the twenty-ninth year of the Duke's reign,
the Duke was in Chǔ.
Why is it said that the Duke was in Chǔ?
The first month is mentioned to preserve the ruler.
9.29.2 In the fifth month of summer,
the Duke returned from Chǔ.
9.29.3 On the Gēngwǔ day,
Hóu Kàn of Wèi died.
9.29.4 Kuài assassinated Yúzì, the ruler of Wú.
Who was Kuài?
He was a gatekeeper,
and a penal laborer.
If he was a penal laborer, why is he called Kuài?
Because a penal laborer is not the right person for such an act.
A gentleman does not associate with penal laborers,
for associating with penal laborers is a path to treating death lightly.

9.29.5 Zhòngsūn Jié met with Xún Yíng of Jìn, Gāo Zhǐ of Qí, Huá Dìng of Sòng, Shìshū Qí of Wèi, Gōngsūn Duàn of Zhèng, people from Cáo, people from Jǔ, people from Zhūlóu, people from Téng, people from Xuē, and people from Xiǎozhūlóu to build a city for Qǐ.
9.29.6 The Hóu of Jìn sent Shì Yǎng to pay a formal visit.
9.29.7 Zǐ of Qǐ came to form an alliance.
9.29.8 The Zǐ of Wú sent Zhá to pay a formal visit.
Wú had no ruler and no grand master,
so how could there be a ruler and a grand master here?
It is to praise Jìzǐ.
How was Jìzǐ praiseworthy?
He yielded the state.
How did he yield the state?
Yè, Yújì, and Yímèi, along with Jìzǐ, were four born of the same mother.
Jìzǐ was young but talented,
and his brothers all loved him,
and they all wanted to establish him as the ruler.
Yè said:
"If we were to seize the state now and give it to Jìzǐ,
Jìzǐ still would not accept it.
Let us not give it to our sons but to our younger brothers,
and let brothers take turns being the ruler,
and then pass the state on to Jìzǐ."
They all said:
"Agreed."
Therefore, all those who became rulers
treated death lightly to show their courage,
and they would always offer a prayer before eating and drinking,
saying:
"If Heaven truly intends for Wú to have a state,
may it quickly bring misfortune upon my body."
Therefore, when Yè died,
Yújì was established.
When Yújì died,
Yímèi was established.
When Yímèi died,
the state should have gone to Jìzǐ.
Jìzǐ was on a mission and fled.
Liáo, the eldest son of a concubine,
then took the throne.
Jìzǐ returned from his mission
and arrived to find him ruling.
Hélǘ said:
"The reason why the former ruler did not give the state to his son but to his younger brother
was all for the sake of Jìzǐ.
If we are to follow the former ruler's command,
then the state should belong to Jìzǐ;
but if we are not to follow the former ruler's command,
then I should be the one to be established.
How can Liáo be the ruler?"
Thereupon, he sent Zhuānzhū to assassinate Liáo,
and offer the state to Jìzǐ.
Jìzǐ refused, saying:
"If you assassinate my ruler
and I accept your state,
it would mean that I am conspiring with you.
If you kill my brother,
and I then kill you,
it would mean that fathers, sons, and brothers would kill each other endlessly."
He left for Yánlíng
and never entered the state of Wú for the rest of his life.
Therefore, gentlemen praise his refusal as righteous
and his abstaining from killing as benevolent.
If Jìzǐ was so praiseworthy, then how could Wú have a ruler and a grand master?
By having Jìzǐ as a minister,
it was appropriate to have a ruler.
Who was Zhá?
It was the name of Jìzǐ of Wú.
The *Chūnqiū* does not name virtuous people,
so why is he named here?
To show acceptance of the Yídí does not require consistency.
Jìzǐ is someone to be praised,
so why is he treated as insufficient?
To acknowledge someone as a minister, one must make him a minister;
to acknowledge someone as a son, one must make him a son.
9.29.9 In the ninth month of autumn,
the Duke of Wèi Xiàn was buried.
9.29.10 Gāo Zhǐ of Qí fled to Běiyān.
9.29.11 In winter,
Zhòngsūn Jié went to Jìn.
9.30.1 In the first month of spring, the thirtieth year of the Duke's reign,
the Zǐ of Chǔ sent Wěi Pō to pay a formal visit.
9.30.2 In the fourth month of summer,
the heir apparent Bān of Cài assassinated his ruler, Gù.
9.30.3 On the Jiǎwǔ day of the fifth month,
there was a fire in Sòng,
and Bó Jī died.
9.30.4 The Heavenly King killed his younger brother Niánfū.
9.30.5 Wángzǐ Xiá fled to Jìn.
9.30.6 In the seventh month of autumn,
Shū Gōng went to Sòng to
bury Gòng Jī of Sòng.
The burial of a wife from another state is not usually recorded,
so why is it recorded here?
It is to conceal something.
What is being concealed?
There was a fire in Sòng,
and Bó Jī died there.
Why is she given a posthumous title?
Because she was virtuous.
How was she virtuous?
There was a fire in Sòng,
and Bó Jī was present.
An official repeatedly said:
"The fire has reached us;
please come out."
Bó Jī said:
"I cannot.
I have heard that
a woman does not go out at night
without her attendant, and does not descend from the hall
without her governess.
The attendant has arrived,
but the governess has not yet arrived."
She perished in the fire.
9.30.7 Zhèng Liángxiāo fled to Xǔ,
entered Zhèng from Xǔ,
and the people of Zhèng killed Liángxiāo.
9.30.8 In the tenth month of winter,
the Duke Jǐng of Cài was buried.
Since the perpetrators had not been apprehended,
why is the burial recorded?
It is a renunciation by the gentleman.
9.30.9 The people of Jìn 晉, Qí 齊, Sòng 宋, Wèi 衛, Zhèng 鄭, Cáo 曹, Jǔ 莒, Zhūlóu 邾婁, Téng 滕, Xuē 薛, Qǐ 杞, and Xiǎo Zhūlóu 小邾婁 met at Chányuān 澶淵,
because of a disaster in Sòng 宋.
What was the disaster in Sòng 宋?
The lords met at Chányuān 澶淵,
all for the disaster in Sòng 宋.
The meeting did not yet mention the reason for it,
why does this mention the reason?
To record Bó Jī 伯姬.
The lords gathered together
and replaced what Sòng 宋 had lost,
saying that the dead could not be brought back to life,
but their wealth was restored.
This was a major event,
why was it made insignificant?
It was done by a q卿 (minister).
If it was done by a q卿, then why is the person referred to in this way?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
A q卿 should not be concerned with the affairs of other lords.
9.31.1 In the thirty-first year, spring, the king's first month.
9.31.2 In summer, the sixth month, on the day xīnsì 辛巳,
the Duke died at the Chǔ 楚 Palace.
9.31.3 In autumn, the ninth month, on the day guǐsì 癸巳,
Zǐ Yě 子野 died.
9.31.4 On the day jǐhài 己亥,
Zhòngsūn Jié 仲孫羯 died.
9.31.5 In winter, the tenth month,
the Viscount of Téng 滕 came to attend the funeral.
9.31.6 On the day guǐyǒu 癸酉,
we buried our lord, Duke Xiāng 襄公.
9.31.7 In the eleventh month,
the people of Jǔ 莒 assassinated their lord, Mìzhōu 密州.
10.1.1 In the first year, spring, the king's first month,
the Duke ascended the throne.

10.1.2 Shūsūn Bào 叔孫豹 met with Zhào Wǔ 趙武 of Jìn 晉, Gōngzǐ Wéi 公子圍 of Chǔ 楚, Guó Zhuó 國酌 of Qí 齊, Xiàng Xù 向戌 of Sòng 宋, Shí È 石惡 of Wèi 衛, Gōngzǐ Zhāo 公子招 of Chén 陳, Gōngsūn Guīshēng 公孫歸生 of Cài 蔡, Xuān Hǔ 軒虎 of Zhèng 鄭, and the people of Xǔ 許 and Cáo 曹 at Huò 漷.
This was Zhāo 招, the younger brother of the Marquis of Chén 陳.
Why is he not referred to as "younger brother"?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
It is a demotion because he killed the Heir Apparent Yǎnshī 偃師,
saying that Zhāo 招, the younger brother of the Marquis of Chén 陳, killed the Heir Apparent Yǎnshī 偃師 of Chén 陳.
When senior officers kill each other, they are referred to by their personal names.
Why is he referred to by his name and clan name when he killed?
It indicates that from then on, he would assassinate the lord.
Now, when you lead [an army],
why is the wording the same as for those who assassinate their relatives?
There should be no leading of armies regarding lords and relatives;
if they lead an army, they must be punished.
Then why was he not demoted for his assassination?
Because the crime of assassinating a relative is so severe,
the *Chūnqiū* does not wait for a demotion;
for cases where the crime is evident from the severance [of relations],
the severance itself is enough to show the crime without a demotion.
For cases where the crime becomes evident only after a demotion and severance [of relations],
a demotion and severance are used to show the crime.
Now, Zhāo's 招 crime is already severe,
why is he demoted again here?
To emphasize Zhāo's 招 guilt.
How is Zhāo's 招 guilt emphasized?
It indicates that Chǔ 楚 used the pretext of punishing Zhāo 招 to destroy Chén 陳.
10.1.3 In the third month, [they] took Yùn 運.
What is Yùn 運?
It is a town within [our] territory.
Why does it say "[they] took it"?
Because [we] did not listen [to them].
10.1.4 In summer,
Zhēn 鍼, the younger brother of the Earl of Qín 秦, fled to Jìn 晉.
Qín 秦 did not have senior officers,
why is this recorded?
Because he served in Jìn 晉.
Why did he serve in Jìn 晉?
Because [the Earl] had a state with a thousand chariots
and could not accommodate his own younger brother,
therefore, gentlemen consider it a flight.
10.1.5 In the sixth month, on the day dīngsì 丁巳,
Zǐ Huá 子華 of Zhūlóu 邾婁 died.
10.1.6 Xún Wú 荀吳 of Jìn 晉 led troops and defeated the Dí 狄 at Dàyuán 大原.
This was Dà Lǔ 大鹵.
Why is it called Dàyuán 大原?
The land and its products follow the Central States,
and the local people's names follow their rulers.
What is a yuán 原?
A level surface above is called a yuán 原,
and a level surface below is called a xí 隰.
10.1.7 In autumn,
Jǔ Qùjí 莒去疾 entered Jǔ 莒 from Qí 齊.
10.1.8 Jǔ Zhǎn 莒展 fled to Wú 吳.
10.1.9 Shū Gōng 叔弓 led troops to demarcate the fields of Yùn 運.
What does "demarcate the fields of Yùn 運" mean?
It means establishing borders with Jǔ 莒.
If it means establishing borders with Jǔ 莒,
then why lead troops there?
Because [we] feared Jǔ 莒.
10.1.10 [We] buried Duke Dào 悼公 of Zhūlóu 邾婁.
10.1.11 In winter, the eleventh month, on the day jǐyǒu 己酉,
Zǐ Juǎn 子卷 of Chǔ 楚 died.
10.1.12 Gōngzǐ Bǐ 公子比 of Chǔ 楚 fled to Jìn 晉.
10.2.1 In the second year, spring,
the Marquis of Jìn 晉 sent Hán Qǐ 韓起 to come and offer gifts.
10.2.2 In summer,
Shū Gōng 叔弓 went to Jìn 晉.
10.2.3 In autumn,
Zhèng 鄭 killed its senior officer, Gōngsūn Hēi 公孫黑.
10.2.4 In winter,
the Duke went to Jìn 晉 but returned at the Hé 河 (Yellow River).
What does "returned at the Hé 河" mean?
It means [he] did not dare to proceed.

and Wú 吳 enfeoffed him at Fáng 防.

Because [the text] does not approve of lords independently granting fiefs.

The son of a ruler who was punished is not established.
It was not out of anger,
but because there was no successor.

He was used to build defenses.

Qí Gāo Yǎn (齊高偃) led an army to install the Earl of Běiyān (北燕伯) at Yáng (陽).

The Master said:
"I already know this."
Those at his side said:
"If you already know it,
why not change it?"
He said:
"What if you do not know?
The *Chūnqiū* (春秋) is a faithful history.

As for its wording, Qiū (丘) alone is at fault."

This was the murder of his ruler,
why does it say "returned"?
"Returned" implies no wickedness in murdering and ascending to the throne.
Why does "returned" imply no wickedness in murdering and ascending to the throne?
Língwáng (靈王) acted immorally,
building the Terrace of Gānqī (乾谿)
for three years without completion.
Chǔ Gōngzǐ Qìjí (楚公子棄疾) coerced Bǐ (比) and established him.

those who return late will not regain their fields and villages."
The multitude dispersed and left,
and Língwáng (靈王) committed suicide by hanging.
Chǔ Gōngzǐ Qìjí (楚公子棄疾) murdered Gōngzǐ Bǐ (公子比).
Bǐ (比) had already been established,
why is he called *gōngzǐ* (公子)?

If his intention was improper,
then why add "murdered him"?
It was fitting for Bǐ (比) to have died for righteousness rather than be established.
When grandees kill each other, they are referred to by "person,"

It means he was about to become ruler from that point on.

the Duke met with Liú Zǐ (劉子), Jìn Hóu (晉侯), Qí Hóu (齊侯), Sòng Gōng (宋公), Wèi Hóu (衛侯), Zhèng Bó (鄭伯), Cáo Bó (曹伯), Jǔ Zǐ (莒子), Zhūlóu Zǐ (邾婁子), Téng Zǐ (滕子), Xuē Bó (薛伯), Qǐ Bó (杞伯), and Xiǎozhūlóu Zǐ (小邾婁子) at Píngqiū (平丘).

they formed an alliance at Píngqiū (平丘).
The Duke did not participate in the alliance,
and the Jìn (晉) people seized Jìsūn Yǐnrú (季孫隱如) and took him back.
The Duke returned from the meeting.
Why did the Duke not participate in the alliance?
The Duke was not allowed to participate in the alliance.
If the Duke was not allowed to participate in the alliance,
and a grandee was seized,
why attend the meeting?
There was no shame in it.
Why no shame?
When the feudal lords caused chaos,
and restored Chén (陳) and Cài (蔡), the *jūnzǐ* (君子) felt no shame in not participating.

Chén Hóu Wú (陳侯吳) returned to Chén (陳).

In winter, in the tenth month,
Cài Línggōng (蔡靈公) was buried.
The Duke went to Jìn (晉),
reached the Hé (河), then returned.

When a senior official hears of the death of the ruler,

Zhǐ administered medicine, which killed him.
If Zhǐ administered medicine, which killed him, then why is it termed an assassination?
It is a criticism of the Crown Prince's incomplete filial piety.
How is it a criticism of the Crown Prince's incomplete filial piety?
It is said:
"When Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn attended to an illness,
one more mouthful of rice would cause a sudden recovery,
one less mouthful of rice would cause a sudden recovery,
one more layer of clothing would cause a sudden recovery,
one less layer of clothing would cause a sudden recovery."
Zhǐ administered medicine, which killed him,
therefore the noble man added "assassination,"
saying:
"Shìzǐ Zhǐ of Xǔ assassinated his ruler, Mǎi,
is the noble man's judgment of Zhǐ.
The burial of Duke Dào of Xǔ
is the noble man's pardon of Zhǐ.
Pardoning Zhǐ
is to excuse Zhǐ from the crime."

Gōngsūn Huì of Cáo fled from Méng to Sòng.

If it was a betrayal, then why is the betrayal not mentioned?
It is to avoid naming the shame of Gōngzǐ Xǐshí 时 later,
for the *Chūnqiū* avoids naming the shame of the virtuous.
How was Gōngzǐ Xǐshí 喜时 virtuous?
He yielded the state.
How did he yield the state?
When Bólú of Cáo died in the army,
it was not known whether Gōngzǐ Xǐshí 时 was following,
or whether Gōngzǐ Fùchú 負芻 was following;
one could have become the ruler in the state,
or one could have become the leader in the army.
When Gōngzǐ Xǐshí 时 saw that Gōngzǐ Fùchú 負芻 was about to become the ruler,
he hesitated and withdrew.
If Gōngzǐ Xǐshí 时 was virtuous, then why is the shame of Huì avoided?
The noble man's praise of the good is long-lasting,
and his condemnation of the evil is short-lived;
condemnation of evil stops with the person himself,
and praise of good extends to his descendants.
Because the descendants of the virtuous
are worthy, the noble man avoids naming their shame.

It was a repulsive illness.

What were the southern suburbs of Sòng?
It was like Yīn Zhū.
10.21.4 In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, ré-wǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
10.21.5 In the eighth month, yǐ-hài,
Shū Cuó died.
winter,
Marquis Zhū of Cài fled to Chǔ.
The Duke went to Jìn,
reaching the Hé,
then returned.
10.22.1 In the spring of the twenty-second year,
the Marquis of Qí attacked Jǔ.
10.22.2 Huá Hài, Xiàng Níng, and Huá Dìng of Sòng fled from the southern suburbs of Sòng to Chǔ.
There was a great hunt at Chāng Jiān.
10.22.4 In summer, the fourth month, yǐ-chǒu,
the Heavenly King died.
In the sixth month,
Shū Yǎng went to the capital.
The Jing King was buried.
The royal house was in disorder.
Why is it said that the royal house was in disorder?
It did not involve outsiders.
Liú Zǐ and Dān Zǐ installed Wáng Měng at Huáng.
Why is he called Wáng Měng?
He was in charge of the state.
autumn,
Liú Zǐ and Dān Zǐ brought Wáng Měng into the royal city.
What was the royal city?
It was Xī Zhōu.
Why does it say "brought in"?
It was a usurping expression.
In the tenth month of winter,
Wángzǐ Měng died.
This was a ruler who did not even last a year,
why is it said that Wángzǐ Měng died?
He was not properly appointed.
Not being properly appointed
means not according to the succession of father dying and son succeeding,
or elder brother dying and younger brother taking over.
10.22.9 On the first day of the twelfth month, guǐ-yǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
10.23.1 In the spring of the twenty-third year, the royal first month,
Shū Sūn Shě went to Jìn.
On guǐ-chǒu,
Shū Yǎng died.
The people of Jìn detained our envoy Shū Sūn Shě.
The people of Jìn besieged Jiāo.
What is Jiāo?
It is the capital of the Son of Heaven.
Why is it not attached to Zhōu?
It does not involve attacking the Son of Heaven.
summer, the sixth month,
Marquis Dōng Guó of Cài died in Chǔ.
autumn, the seventh month,
Gēng Yú, the Zi of Jǔ, came to seek refuge.
On wù-chén,
Wú defeated the forces of Dùn, Hú, Shěn, Cài, Chén, and Xǔ at Jīfù.
Zǐ Kūn of Hú and Zǐ Yíng of Shěn were extinguished,
and Xià Niè of Chén was captured.
This was a partial battle,
why is it described with the language of a deceitful battle?
It does not allow the barbarians to rule the Central Kingdom.
Then why not have the Central Kingdom rule it?
The Central Kingdom is also newly barbarian.
What do the words "extinguished" and "captured" mean?
They distinguish between ruler and minister.
A ruler dying in office is called "extinguished,"
and being captured alive is called "captured";
for grand officers, death or life are both called "captured."
It does not allow the barbarians to rule the Central Kingdom,
then what does it mean by saying Xià Niè of Chén was captured?
Wú had made little progress.
The Heavenly King resided at Díquán.
This had not been three years,
why is it called the Heavenly King?
It acknowledges there was a Son of Heaven,
and Yǐn Shì established Wángzǐ Zhāo.
In the eighth month, yǐ-wèi,
there was an earthquake.
winter,
the Duke went to Jìn,
reaching the Hé.
The Duke became ill
and then returned.
Why is it said that the Duke became ill and then returned?
It was to avoid shame.
10.24.1 In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, the royal second month, bǐng-xū,
Zhòng Sūn Jué died.
Shě returned from Jìn.
10.24.3 In summer, the fifth month, yǐ-wèi, the first day,
there was a solar eclipse.
autumn, the eighth month,
there was a great rain sacrifice.
On dīng-yǒu,
Bó Yùlì of Qǐ died.
winter,
Wú extinguished Cháo.
The Ping Duke of Qǐ was buried.
10.25.1 In the spring of the twenty-fifth year,
Shū Sūn Shě went to Sòng.
summer,

Shū Ní met with Zhào Yāng of Jìn, Yuè Shìxīn of Sòng, Běigōng Xǐ of Wèi, Yóu Jí of Zhèng, people from Cáo, people from Zhūlóu, people from Téng, people from Xuē, and people from Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Huángfǔ.
Storks and mynas came to nest.
Why is it written down?
To record something unusual.
What is unusual about it?
They are not birds of the Central Kingdom,
they should nest in holes but instead built nests.
autumn, the seventh month, shàng-xīn, there was a great rain sacrifice, and jì-xīn, there was another rain sacrifice.
What was the "another rain sacrifice"?
"Another rain sacrifice" was not actually a rain sacrifice,
but a gathering of people to drive out the Jì family.
the ninth month, jǐ-hài,
the Duke went to Qí,
stopping at Yángzhōu.
10.25.6 Qí Hóu offered condolences to the duke at Yějǐng.
What is meant by "offered condolences to the duke"?
Zhāo Gōng was about to assassinate the Jìshì.
He told Zǐjiā Jū:
"The Jìshì are behaving without principle,
having usurped the ducal house for a long time.
I wish to assassinate them; what do you think?"
Zǐjiā Jū said:
"The feudal lords have been usurping the Son of Heaven,
and the grand masters have been usurping the feudal lords,
for a long time."
Zhāo Gōng said:
"In what way have I usurped?"
Zǐjiā Jū said:
"Setting up two watchtowers,
riding in a *dàlù* carriage,
using red shields
and jade axes
to perform the *Dàxià* dance,
and using eight rows of dancers to perform the *Dàwǔ* dance—
all these are rites of the Son of Heaven.
Moreover, cattle and horses
are submissive because they are well-fed;
the Jìshì have already won the people's hearts for a long time;
Your Lordship should not disgrace yourself too much."
Zhāo Gōng did not heed his words
and eventually assassinated them, but was defeated.
He fled to Qí.
The Qí Hóu offered condolences to the duke at Yějǐng,
saying:
"Why did Your Lordship abandon the altars of the state of Lǔ?"
Zhāo Gōng said:
"The unfortunate man was incompetent
and failed to protect the altars of the state of Lǔ,
bringing shame upon you."
He bowed twice, touching his forehead to the ground.
Then, he congratulated Zǐjiā Jū, saying:
"Zǐ saved me from a great disaster."
Zǐjiā Jū said:
"Your servant was incompetent
and led you into a great disaster.
Your Lordship could not bear to punish me with the axe and block,
and instead grants me death."
He bowed twice,
touching his forehead to the ground.
Gāo Zǐ held a bamboo basket with food and four pieces of dried meat,
and Guó Zǐ held a jug of broth,
saying:
"Our humble ruler has heard that Your Lordship is abroad,
and that the evening meal has not yet been prepared.
We dare to present these provisions to your followers."
Zhāo Gōng said:
"Your Lordship does not forget my late lord
and extends your kindness to this unfortunate man,
bestowing upon him a great honor."
He bowed twice, kowtowing, and received the gifts with his sleeve.
Gāo Zǐ said:
"There is something inauspicious about this;
Your Lordship should not deign to accept such a great honor."
Zhāo Gōng performed the sacrifice but did not taste the food.
Jǐng Gōng said:
"I have the humble garments of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared to wear.
I have the humble vessels of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared to use.
I dare to offer them to you."
Zhāo Gōng said:
"The unfortunate man was incompetent
and failed to protect the altars of the state of Lǔ,
bringing shame upon you.
I dare not accept such a great honor;
I dare to decline."
Jǐng Gōng said:
"I have the humble garments of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared to wear;
I have the humble vessels of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared to use.
I dare to insist on offering them to you."
Zhāo Gōng said:
"Because my ancestral temples are in Lǔ,
I have the garments of my late lord,
but I am not able to wear them;
I have the vessels of my late lord,
but I am not able to bring them out.
I dare to firmly decline."
Jǐng Gōng said:
"I have the humble garments of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared to wear;
I have the humble vessels of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared to use.
May I offer them to your followers?"
Zhāo Gōng said:
"What title should this unfortunate man have?"
Jǐng Gōng said:
"Which ruler is without a title?"
Thereupon, Zhāo Gōng wailed and wept,
and all the grand masters wept.
After weeping,
they used people as mats,
used curtains as cushions,
and used saddles as rests,
and met each other with the proper etiquette.
Confucius said: "The rites and words were worth seeing!"
10.25.7 In the tenth month, *dōng*, on the day *wùchén*, Shūsūn Shě died.
10.25.8 In the eleventh month,
on the day *jǐhài*, Sòng Gōng Zuǒ died at Qūjí.
What is meant by "Qūjí"?
It is a city of Sòng.
When a feudal lord dies within his territory, it is not recorded as "dying at [place]".
Why is it recorded as "dying at [place]" in this case?
It is because of concern for the interior [of the state].
10.25.9 In the twelfth month,
the Qí Hóu took Yùn.
Why is the taking of a city outside not recorded?
Why is it recorded in this case?
It is because he took it for the duke.
10.26.1 In the twenty-sixth year, in spring, the royal first month,
the funeral of Sòng Yuán Gōng took place.
10.26.2 In the third month,
the duke arrived from Qí
and resided at Yùn.
10.26.3 In summer,
the duke besieged Chéng.
10.26.4 In autumn,
the duke met with the Qí Hóu, the Jǔ Zǐ, the Zhūlóu Zǐ, and the Qǐ Bó to form an alliance at Tuánlíng.
The duke arrived from the meeting
and resided at Yùn.
10.26.5 In the ninth month, on the day *gēngshēn*, Chǔ Zǐ Jū died.
10.26.6 In the tenth month,
the Heavenly King entered Chéngzhōu.
What is meant by "Chéngzhōu"?
It is Dōngzhōu.
Why does it say "entered"?
It is without suspicion [of usurpation].
Yǐn Shì, Shào Bó, and Máo Bó fled to Chǔ with Wángzǐ Cháo.
10.27.1 In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the duke went to Qí.
The duke arrived from Qí
and resided at Yùn.
10.27.2 In the fourth month of summer,
Wú assassinated their lord, Liáo.
10.27.3 Chǔ killed their grand master, Xì Wǎn.
10.27.4 In autumn,
Jìn Shì Yǎng, Sòng Lè Qílí, Wèi Běigōng Xǐ, the men of Cáo, the men of Zhūlóu, and the men of Téng met at Hù.
In the tenth month of winter,
Cáo Bó Wǔ died.
10.27.5 Zhūlóu Kuài came to seek refuge.
What is Zhūlóu Kuài?
He is a grand master of Zhūlóu.
Zhūlóu did not have grand masters.
Why is this recorded?
It is recorded because he was close [to the event].
10.27.6 The duke went to Qí.
The duke arrived from Qí
and resided at Yùn.
10.28.1 In the twenty-eighth year, in spring, the royal third month,
the funeral of Cáo Dào Gōng took place.
10.28.2 The duke went to Jìn
and stopped at Gānhóu.
10.28.3 In the fourth month of summer, on the day *bǐngxū*, Zhèng Bó Níng died.
10.28.4 In the sixth month,
the funeral of Zhèng Dìng Gōng took place.
10.28.5 In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *guǐsì*, Téng Zǐ Níng died.
In winter,
the Dàogōng of Téng was buried.
10.29.1 In the spring of the twenty-ninth year,
the Duke returned from Gānhóu
and resided in Yùn.
10.29.2 The Hóu of Qí sent Gāo Zhāng to offer condolences to the Duke.
10.29.3 The Duke went to Jìn
and stayed at Gānhóu.
10.29.4 In summer, the fourth month, on Gēngzǐ day,
Shū Ní died.
10.29.5 In autumn, the seventh month.
10.29.6 In winter, the tenth month,
Yùn collapsed.
Why does the text not use "collapsed" for a city?
It is a walled suburb that collapsed.
Why say "walled suburb"?
Because the ruler was residing there.
10.30.1 In the thirtieth year, spring, the royal first month,
the Duke was at Gānhóu.
10.30.2 In summer, the sixth month, on Gēngchén day,
the Hóu of Jìn, Qùjí, died.
10.30.3 In autumn, the eighth month,
the Qīnggōng of Jìn was buried.
10.30.4 In winter, the twelfth month,
Wú destroyed Xú,
and Zǐ Zhāng Yǔ of Xú fled to Chǔ.
10.31.1 In the thirty-first year, spring, the royal first month,
the Duke was at Gānhóu.
10.31.2 Jìsūn Yǐnrú met Xún Lì of Jìn at Shìlì.
10.31.3 In summer, the fourth month, on Dīngsì day,
Bó Gǔ of Xuē died.
10.31.4 The Hóu of Jìn sent Xún Lì to offer condolences to the Duke at Gānhóu.
10.31.5 In autumn,
the Xiàngōng of Xuē was buried.
10.31.6 In winter,
Hēi Gōng fled with làn to our state.
Why does the text omit Zhūlóu?
Because làn was generally accessible.
Why was làn generally accessible?
Because descendants of worthy men ought to have land.
Who is considered a worthy man?
Shū Shù is considered a worthy man.
Why is Shū Shù considered worthy?
Because he yielded the state.
How did he yield the state?
At the time of Zhūlóu Yán,
a daughter of Zhūlóu became a lady of Lǔ;
was it then unknown whether she was the wife of Duke Wǔ or
Duke Yī?
When Xiàogōng was young,
Yán debauched nine young masters in the palace,
and consequently brought in bandits;
was it then unknown whether they were young masters of Lǔ or
young masters of Zhūlóu?
The mother of Zāng, she was the one who raised the Duke.
When the ruler is young, there ought to be someone to raise him,
but with the concubine of a grand master
and the wife of a gentleman,
is it then unknown what the mother of Zāng was doing?
The one who raised the Duke certainly had her son enter to raise him.
The mother of Zāng heard there were bandits,
so she exchanged her son for the Duke,
carried the Duke and fled,
and when the bandits arrived,
they approached the Duke's bedchamber and murdered him.
The ministers Bào Guǎngfù and Liáng Mǎizi heard there were bandits
and hastened to arrive.
The mother of Zāng said,
"The Duke is not dead;
he is here;
I have exchanged my son for the Duke."
Thereupon, she carried Xiàogōng and went to Zhōu to appeal to the Son of Heaven,
and the Son of Heaven punished Yán on his behalf and established Shū Shù,
and returned Xiàogōng to Lǔ.
Madam Yán was the daughter of Ǒuyíng, a woman of surpassing beauty.
She said,
"If anyone can kill Shā Yán for me,
I will be his wife."
Shū Shù killed Shā Yán for her
and took her as his wife,
and they had a son named Xū.
Xià Fù, he had been employed by Yán.
When Xū was young,
they all loved him;
when they ate, they would certainly have the two sons sit beside them when they ate,
and if there was rare or exotic food,
Xū would certainly take his fill first.
Xià Fù said,
"Since coming here,
Xū has more than enough while others do not have enough."
Shū Shù became aware of it
and said,
"Ah!
This is truly your state!"
He arose and offered the state to Xià Fù,
but Xià Fù accepted it and divided it in half.
Shū Shù said,
"That will not do!"
He divided it into thirds.
Shū Shù said,
"That will not do!"
He divided it into fourths.
Shū Shù said,
"That will not do!"
He divided it into fifths,
and only then did Xià Fù accept it.
Gōng Hùzǐ, he was a father and elder brother of Zhūlóu,
and he was familiar with the affairs of Zhūlóu;
he said,
"How could anyone speak of another's state as worthy to this extent!"
At the time of punishing Yán,
the Son of Heaven died,
and Shū Shù arose and offered the state to Xià Fù.
At that time,
the people of Zhūlóu were constantly under arms from Zhōu,
saying,
"Why did you kill our Son of Heaven?"
If làn was generally accessible, then why does the text omit Zhūlóu?
Nowhere in the world was làn generally accessible.
If nowhere in the world was làn generally accessible,
then why does the text say that he fled with làn?
Shū Shù was a worthy grand master;
if we cut him off, then it would be that Shū Shù did not want to cut him off;
if we do not cut him off, then he would be a hereditary grand master;
it is not proper for the righteousness of a grand master to be hereditary;
therefore, it is pushed through generally in this case.
10.31.7 On the first day of the twelfth month, Xīnhài,
there was a solar eclipse.
10.32.1 In the thirty-second year, spring, the royal first month,
the Duke was at Gānhóu.
10.32.2 We took Kǎn.
What is Kǎn?
It is a city of Zhūlóu.
Why is it not linked to Zhūlóu?
To avoid mentioning the frequency.
10.32.3 In summer,
Wú attacked Yuè.
10.32.4 In autumn, the seventh month.
10.32.5 In winter,

Zhòngsūn Hējì met Hán Bùxìn of Jìn, Gāo Zhāng of Qí, Zhòng Jǐ of Sòng, Shìshū Shēn of Wèi, Guó Shēn of Zhèng, men of Cáo, men of Jǔ, men of Zhūlóu, men of Xuē, men of Qǐ, and men of Xiǎo Zhūlóu to build the city of Chéngzhōu.
10.32.6 On Jǐwèi day, the twelfth month,
the Duke died at Gānhóu.
11.1.1 In the first year, spring, the royal [month].
Why does Dìng lack the first month?
The first month is when he properly ascended the throne.
The reason Dìng lacks the first month is that he ascended the throne later;
why was it later when he ascended the throne?
Because Zhāogōng was abroad,
and whether he could enter or not was still unknown.
Why was it still unknown?
It depended on the Jì clan.
Dìng and Āi often used subtle language;
the master was accustomed to reading it and asking about its transmission,
so it was unknown whether he himself was guilty.
In the third month,
the people of Jìn 晉 captured Sòng Zhòngjǐ 宋仲幾 in the capital.
What was Zhòngjǐ's 仲幾 crime?
Not weakening the city walls.
What does "he spoke in the capital" mean?
It means "the Earl punished him."
If it means "the Earl punished him," then why does it call him "a man"?
A degradation.
Why a degradation?
Because he did not exclusively capture him with the Dàfū 大夫.
Why "did not"?
In reality, he did, but the text says he did not.
Why does the text say he did not?
It is the proper conduct of a Dàfū 大夫 not to exclusively capture him.
In the sixth month, on guǐhài 癸亥 day,
the Duke's funeral procession arrived from Gānhóu 乾侯.
On wùchén 戊辰 day,
the Duke ascended the throne.
Since the Duke's funeral procession arrived from Gānhóu 乾侯 on guǐhài 癸亥 day,
then why did he ascend the throne on wùchén 戊辰 day?
He adjusted the coffin between the two pillars,
and then ascended the throne.
Zǐ Shěnzǐ 子沈子 said:
"Stabilize the ruler in the state,
and then ascend the throne."
Ascending the throne is not a matter of choosing a day;
why is a day recorded here?
It is recorded internally.
In the seventh month, on guǐsì 癸巳 day,
we buried our lord, Duke Zhāo 昭公.
In the ninth month,
there was a grand rain prayer.
They established the Yáng Gōng 煬宮.
What is the Yáng Gōng 煬宮?
It is the palace of Duke Yáng 煬公.
What does "established" mean?
"Established" means it should not have been established;
establishing the Yáng Gōng 煬宮 was contrary to ritual.
In the tenth month of winter,
fallen frost killed the beans.
Why is it written?
To record a prodigy.
This was a disaster for the beans;
why is it written as a prodigy?
A prodigy is greater than a disaster.
In the second year, in the first month of spring, the King....
In the fifth month, on rénchén 壬辰 day,
the Pheasant Gate and the two watchtowers were destroyed by fire.
Why does it say "the Pheasant Gate and the two watchtowers were destroyed by fire"?
The two watchtowers were insignificant.
Then why does it not say, "the Pheasant Gate was destroyed by fire, and the two watchtowers"?
The principal cause of the disaster was the two watchtowers.
If the principal cause of the disaster was the two watchtowers,
then why are they mentioned last?
So as not to attribute a great event to something insignificant.
Why is it written?
To record a disaster.
In autumn,
the people of Chǔ 楚 attacked Wú 吳.
In the tenth month of winter,
the Pheasant Gate and the two watchtowers were newly built.
Why does it say "newly built"?
Because the repairs were extensive.
Repairing something old is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
To censure.
What is being censured?
That they did not attend to the public affairs.
In the third year, in the first month of spring, the King,
the Duke went to Jìn 晉,
but returned at the Hé 河 river.
In the third month, on xīnmǎo 辛卯 day,
Zhulóu Zichuan 邾婁子穿 died.
In the fourth month of summer.
In autumn,
they buried Duke Zhuāng of Zhūlóu 邾婁莊公.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn Hējì 仲孫何忌 and the Viscount of Zhūlóu 邾婁子 made a covenant at Zhī 枝.
In the fourth year, in the second month of spring, the King, on guǐsì 癸巳 day,
Hóu Wú 侯吳 of Chén 陳 died.
In the third month,

the Duke met with Liú Zǐ 劉子, the Marquis of Jìn 晉, Duke of Sòng 宋, Marquis of Cài 蔡, Marquis of Wèi 衛, Viscount of Chén 陳, Earl of Zhèng 鄭, Baron of Xǔ 許, Earl of Cáo 曹, Viscount of Jǔ 莒, Viscount of Zhūlóu 邾婁子, Viscount of Dùn 頓, Viscount of Hú 胡, Viscount of Téng 滕, Earl of Xuē 薛, Earl of Qǐ 杞, Xia of Qí 齊, at Zhàolíng 召陵,
and invaded Chǔ 楚.
In the fourth month of summer, on gēngchén 庚辰 day,
Gōngsūn Guīxìng 公孫歸姓 of Cài 蔡 led troops and destroyed Shěn 沈,
brought back Zǐ Jiā 子嘉 of Shěn 沈,
and killed him.
In the fifth month,
the Duke and the feudal lords made a covenant at Hàoyóu 浩油.
Earl Wù 戊 of Qǐ 杞 died at the meeting.
In the sixth month,
they buried Duke Huì of Chén 陳惠公.
Xǔ 許 moved to Róngchéng 容城.
In the seventh month of autumn,
the Duke returned from the meeting.
Liú Juǎn 劉卷 died.
Who was Liú Juǎn 劉卷?
He was a Dàfū 大夫 of the Son of Heaven.
The death of an external Dàfū 大夫 is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
Because we are his host.
They buried Duke Dào of Qǐ 杞悼公.
The people of Chǔ 楚 besieged Cài 蔡.
Shì Yǎng 士鞅 of Jìn 晉 and Kǒng Yǔ 孔圄 of Wèi 衛 led troops to attack Xiānyú 鮮虞.
They buried Liú Wéngōng 劉文公.
The burial of an external Dàfū 大夫 is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
To record our host.
In the eleventh month, *gēngwǔ*, the Marquis of *Cài* fought with the Viscount of *Wú* and the men of *Chǔ* at *Bójǔ*,
and the *Chǔ* army was utterly defeated.
Why is *Wú* called a viscount?
Because he was a barbarian, yet he worried about the Central States.
How did he worry about the Central States?
*Wǔ Zǐxū*'s father was killed by *Chǔ*,
so he fled *Chǔ* with his bow
and sought out *Hélǘ*.
*Hélǘ* said,
"This man is exceedingly brave
and courageous.
I will raise an army for him and avenge him on *Chǔ*."
*Wǔ Zǐxū* replied,
"The lords of the states do not raise armies for commoners.
Moreover, I have heard that
serving a lord is like serving a father.
To fail in one's duty to one's lord
in order to avenge one's father
is something I will not do."
So he stopped.
*Cài Zhāogōng* gave audience at *Chǔ*.
He had a beautiful fur coat,
*Náng Wǎ* asked for it,
*Zhāogōng* would not give it to him.
Because of this, he detained *Zhāogōng* in *Nányǐng*
for several years
before returning him.

On jiǎxū,
Guó Shū of Qí led troops and fought with Wú at Àilíng;
the Qí troops were utterly defeated,
and Guó Shū of Qí was captured.
In autumn, the seventh month, on xīnyǒu,
the mother of Zǐ Yú of Téng died.
In winter, the eleventh month,
Yǐn Gōng of Téng was buried.
Shìshū Qí of Wèi fled to Sòng.
In the twelfth year, spring,
they used the field tax.
Why is it written?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
Criticizing the initial use of the field tax.
In summer, the fifth month, jiǎ chén day,
Mèngzǐ died.
Who was Mèngzǐ?
The wife of Duke Zhāo.
Why is she called Mèngzǐ?
To avoid marrying someone with the same surname,
she was probably a woman from Wú.
The Duke met with Wú at Tuógāo.
In autumn,
the Duke met with Marquis Wèi, Sòng Huáng Yuàn at Yùn.
Sòng Xiàng Cháo led troops to attack Zhèng.
In winter, the twelfth month, locusts.
Locusts.
Why is it written?
To record a strange occurrence.
What was strange?
It was out of season.
In the thirteenth year, spring,
Zhèng Xuān Dá led troops to capture the Sòng troops at Yán.
Why does it say "capture"?
It was easy.
How was it easy?
Through feigned defection.
In summer,
Lord Xǔ Xū died.
The Duke met with Marquis Jìn and the Viscount of Wú at Huángchí.
Why is Wú called "Viscount"?
Wú was the host of the meeting.
If Wú was the host, why mention Marquis Jìn first?
Because he would not rank the ruler of a barbarian tribe with the central states.
Why mention "and the Viscount of Wú"?
It is the language of a meeting between two hegemons.
If he would not rank the ruler of a barbarian tribe with the central states,
then why use the language of a meeting between two hegemons to mention him?
To emphasize Wú.
Why emphasize Wú?
Because if Wú was there, then none of the lords of the world would dare not come.
The Viscount Shēn of Chǔ led troops to attack Chén.
The people of Yuè invaded Wú.
In autumn,
the Duke returned from the meeting.
Jìn Wèi Duō led troops to invade Wèi.
This was Jìn Wèi Mànduō,
why call him Jìn Wèi Duō?
Criticizing the use of two names,
two names is against propriety.
The burial of Duke Yuán of Xǔ.
In the ninth month, locusts.
Locusts.
In winter, the eleventh month,
a comet appeared in the east.
What is a bó star?
A comet.
Why does it say "in the east"?
It was seen at dawn.
Why is it written?
To record a strange occurrence.
Robbers killed Chén Xià Gōufū.
In the twelfth month, locusts.
Locusts.
In the fourteenth year, spring,
hunting in the west, a lín was captured.
Why is it written?
To record a strange occurrence.
What was strange?
It was not a beast of the central states.
Then who hunted it?
A woodcutter.
If it was a woodcutter, then it was someone insignificant, so
why is it written using the word "hunt"?
To magnify it.
Why magnify it?
To magnify the capture of the lín.
Why magnify the capture of the lín?
The lín is a beast of benevolence.
It appears when there is a true king,
and does not appear when there is no true king.
Someone reported, saying:
"There is a roe deer with a horn."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"For whom has it come!
For whom has it come!"
He wiped his face with his sleeve,
and tears wet his robe.
When Yán Yuān died,
the Master said:
"Alas!
Heaven is destroying me."
When Zǐlù died,
the Master said:
"Alas! Heaven is cutting me off."
When a lín was captured during a hunt in the west,
Kǒngzǐ said:
"My Way is exhausted."
Why does the *Chūnqiū* begin with Duke Yǐn?
Because it records what the ancestors could reach and hear,
where what was seen was recorded differently,
what was heard was recorded differently,
and what was passed down was recorded differently.
Why does it end with the fourteenth year of Duke Āi?
It says:
"It is complete!"
Why does the superior man compose the *Chūnqiū*?
To correct the chaotic world
and return it to righteousness,
nothing is closer to this than the *Chūnqiū*.
Then one may not know if it is right?
Perhaps the superior men delight in the Way of Yáo and Shùn?
In the end, are they not also delighted that Yáo and Shùn knew superior men?
To establish the principles of the *Chūnqiū* to await later sages,
the superior men also find joy in this.
